title: Pareto frontier admits strictly dominated models when prices tie, and which ones is non-deterministic
evidence:
`_pareto_frontier` does `df[...].sort_values("price")` (pandas default kind='quicksort', NOT stable) then keeps a row when `row["quality"] > max_q`. When two models share a price, the arbitrary tie order decides, and the worse one can be appended before the better one is seen.

Reproduced against the live cache with the venv python:

  apply_filters(df, ["Alibaba","SpaceXAI"], 0, "") -> build_pareto_scatter -> the trace named "Pareto Frontier" is:
     $0.1200  20.37 / $0.1375  21.79 / $0.7375  32.13 / $1.3000  39.37 / $5.0000  55.76 / $5.0000  58.08
  The point ($5.00, 55.76) is Grok 4.5 (high); it is strictly dominated by Qwen3.8 Max at the SAME $5.00 with quality 58.08. The line therefore contains a vertical segment, and the label trace also prints "Grok 4.5 (high)" as a frontier model.
  Order fed to the scan after sort_values("price"): Grok 4.5 (high) 55.76, then Qwen3.8 Max 58.08. With kind="stable" it would be Qwen first (and Grok correctly excluded).

Sweep over every reachable filter state:
  - 528 provider filter combos (all singles + all pairs): 3 combos plot a dominated model on the frontier — ('Alibaba','Google'), ('Alibaba','SpaceXAI'), ('Google','NVIDIA').
  - min_quality slider values 5, 10, 20, 30, 45 all plot ($5.00, 55.76); values 0, 15, 25, 35, 40, 50, 55 do not. Pure quicksort nondeterminism — the same data, the same true frontier.
  - Shuffling row order of the FULL undeduped frame 8 times produced 8 DIFFERENT frontier sets, of sizes 11-15, against a true non-dominated set of 10. Extra members were e.g. 'Claude Opus 5 (Adaptive Reasoning, Xhigh Effort)' ($20.00, 62.52), dominated by 'Max Effort' ($20.00, 63.05).

Independently recomputed non-dominated set (minimise price, maximise quality, strict domination) on the deduped unfiltered frame: 10 models, exactly matching the code — so the bug only surfaces on tied prices, which is precisely what filtering exposes. tests/test_pareto_chart.py has 21 tests for this chart and none assert the frontier is the non-dominated set.

Identical implementation at components/charts/animated_pareto.py:27; running it over the real 90-snapshot history plots 11 frontier points for 2026-08-11 where only 10 are non-dominated, including a vertical segment at x=$20.00 (61.48 and 63.05).
user_impact: A user on the Overview tab who ticks Alibaba + SpaceXAI (or just nudges the quality slider to 5) sees Grok 4.5 (high) sitting on the dotted 'Pareto Frontier' line with its name printed beside it — presented as cost/quality-optimal — when Qwen3.8 Max costs exactly the same $5.00/M and scores 2.32 points higher. The frontier line also visibly doubles back vertically, which reads as a rendering glitch. Because the tie order is decided by an unstable sort, the same filter can produce a different frontier on a different data snapshot with no data change to explain it.
suggested_fix: Sort with a deterministic composite key and use non-strict domination: `sub = df[...].sort_values(["price", "quality"], ascending=[True, False], kind="stable")`, then keep a row only when `row["quality"] > max_q` (with the descending-quality secondary key, the first row of each price tie is the only one that can qualify). Add a test asserting the returned set equals a brute-force non-dominated set over the deduped frame and over several tie-heavy filter states. Apply the same fix to animated_pareto.py:27.
verify_reasoning:
Tried to refute by (a) checking for a tie guard elsewhere in _pareto_frontier (components/charts/pareto.py:24-35 — none; the only test is `row["quality"] > max_q` after `sort_values("price")`), (b) checking whether the state is reachable, and (c) re-running the sweep. All of it reproduces.

Ran build_pareto_scatter(apply_filters(df,["Alibaba","SpaceXAI"],0,"")): the 'Pareto Frontier' trace is exactly $0.1200/20.37, $0.1375/21.79, $0.7375/32.13, $1.3000/39.37, $5.0000/55.76, $5.0000/58.08 — two points at the same x, i.e. a vertical segment. Brute-force strict-domination on the same deduped input gives 5 models; the code returns 6; the extra is 'Grok 4.5 (high)' ($5.00, 55.76), dominated by 'Qwen3.8 Max' ($5.00, 58.08). The mode='text' label trace prints 'Grok 4.5 (high)'.

Sweep of all 32 singles + all pairs = 528 combos reproduces the finder's exact result: 3 bad combos, ('Alibaba','Google') and ('Google','NVIDIA') both plotting 'Gemma 4 12B (Reasoning)', ('Alibaba','SpaceXAI') plotting 'Grok 4.5 (high)'. Sort-kind test on that frame: quicksort and heapsort order the $5.00 tie Grok-then-Qwen (frontier size 6, Grok included); stable and mergesort order it Qwen-then-Grok (size 5, Grok excluded).

The reachability is worse than the finder stated. The public site's MIN SCORE control (docs/index.html:48-54) is a fixed dropdown of 0/10/15/20/25/30/35/40/45/50. With NO provider filter at all, ≥10, ≥20, ≥30 and ≥45 each plot the tied pair (5.0, 55.76)+(5.0, 58.08) and each print 'Grok 4.5 (high)' in the frontier label trace. So one click on a primary global filter labels a strictly dominated model as cost/quality-optimal. Unfiltered is correct (code 10 == true 10), which is why docs/figures never showed it.

Two caveats that do not change the verdict: (1) 'non-deterministic' is loose wording — quicksort is deterministic for a given input array, the result is row-order-dependent, not random; (2) the secondary evidence about components/charts/animated_pareto.py:27 is about dead code — `grep -rn animated_pareto` over the repo (excluding venv/__pycache__) and a scan of every .py inside docs/pybundle.zip find zero importers, so that file is vendored but never rendered. The primary claim in pareto.py stands on its own.

Confirmed also that tests/test_pareto_chart.py collects 21 tests and none grep for 'dominat' or assert the frontier equals a non-dominated set.

title: Quadrant zone thresholds and y-axis scale are computed from the filtered frame, so models change quadrant when unrelated filters move
evidence:
`med_speed = plot_df["speed"].median()` and `med_quality = plot_df["quality"].median()` (lines 33-34) are taken from `plot_df`, which is the user-filtered frame passed in by app.py:1090 / static_api.py:223. Same for `y_max = plot_df["quality"].max() * 1.15` (line 55) and `speed_p75 = plot_df["speed"].quantile(0.75)` (line 150).

Measured thresholds from the actual figure (read back off the add_vline/add_hline shapes):
  unfiltered                  n=148  med_speed=105.28  med_quality=25.67
  provider=[OpenAI,Anthropic] n= 36  med_speed= 85.11  med_quality=45.51
  min_quality=40              n= 41  med_speed= 85.11  med_quality=51.58
  search='claude'             n= 11  med_speed= 62.83  med_quality=55.26

Models that change quadrant label versus the unfiltered view:
  provider=[OpenAI,Anthropic]: 5 of 13 plotted models flip. `o3` goes 'Slow · Smart' -> 'Fast · Weak' (BOTH axes invert). 'Claude 4.5 Haiku (Reasoning)' goes 'Fast · Smart' -> 'Fast · Weak'.
  min_quality=40: 12 of 23 flip, e.g. 'Gemini 3.6 Flash (high)', 'Kimi K2.7 Code', 'DeepSeek V4 Pro (Reasoning, Max Effort)' all lose 'Smart'.
  min_quality=20 (a QUALITY-only filter) moves med_speed 105.28 -> 102.7 and flips 19 of 57 models, several on the SPEED axis.
  provider=[Google]: 'Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview' goes 'Fast · Smart' -> 'Slow · Smart'.

y-axis range from the figure: unfiltered [0, 72.51]; provider=Meta [0, 16.65]; search='gemma' [0, 34.14] — the same model sits at a different height depending on who else is on screen.

The codebase already treats this as a bug class everywhere else: quadrant.py:36-39 pins bubble size to BUBBLE_PRICE_REF for exactly this reason, constants.py:255 defines QUALITY_INDEX_MAX 'Fixed so a model keeps the same vertical position ... whatever the filter', local_scatter.py:146 uses `range=[0, QUALITY_INDEX_MAX]`, and tests/test_pareto_chart.py:204 asserts bubble size is invariant under filtering. Nothing asserts the same for the thresholds.
user_impact: A user compares o3 on the Speed vs. Intelligence chart. With no filter it sits in 'Slow · Smart'. They tick two provider checkboxes to narrow the view and the same model — same speed, same score, same bubble — is now sitting in 'Fast · Weak'. The four zone captions are absolute-sounding labels ('Fast · Smart'), so the chart is asserting a categorical judgement about a model that is really a statement about which other rows the user happened to leave visible. Dragging the quality slider also silently moves the speed threshold, which no reader would predict.
suggested_fix: Compute med_speed / med_quality / speed_p75 once from the full catalogue (pass the unfiltered df in, or precompute the thresholds in the caller and hand them to build_quadrant), and set `yaxis.range=[0, QUALITY_INDEX_MAX]` as local_scatter.py already does. Add a test mirroring test_bubble_size_is_invariant_under_filtering that asserts a model's quadrant label is identical for the full frame and a provider-filtered subset.
verify_reasoning:
Tried to refute by looking for a full-frame threshold being passed in from the caller. There is none: app.py:1083 does `filtered = _apply_filters(...)` then app.py:1090 `return build_quadrant(filtered)`, and static_api.py:221-223 does the same for the static site. build_quadrant takes one argument, so it has no access to the unfiltered catalogue.

Read the median crosshairs and y-range straight back off the returned figure (the hline is the shape with yref='y', y0==y1; the vline is xref='x', x0==x1 in log space) and labelled every plotted marker against them:
  unfiltered            n=95  med_speed=105.28  med_q=25.67  yrange=(0, 72.5075)
  prov OpenAI+Anthropic n=13  med_speed= 85.11  med_q=45.51
  minq 40               n=23  med_speed= 85.11  med_q=51.58
  search 'claude'       n= 5  med_speed= 62.83  med_q=55.26
  minq 20               n=57  med_speed=102.70  med_q=37.70
  prov Google           n= 8  med_speed=128.51  med_q=33.56  yrange=(0, 59.317)
  prov Meta             n= 4  med_speed= 38.45  med_q= 9.76  yrange=(0, 16.652)
  search 'gemma'        n= 4  med_speed= 92.89  med_q=24.12  yrange=(0, 34.1435)

Quadrant flips vs. the unfiltered view: OpenAI+Anthropic 6/13 (finder said 5 — minor miscount), including the exact 'o3: Slow · Smart -> Fast · Weak' double-axis inversion and 'Claude 4.5 Haiku (Reasoning): Fast · Smart -> Fast · Weak' they cite. minq 40 flips 13/23; minq 20 — a QUALITY-only filter — moves med_speed 105.28 -> 102.70 and flips 20/57 (finder said 19), several on the SPEED axis. prov Google reproduces 'Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview: Fast · Smart -> Slow · Smart'. Every y-range value they quote matches to the digit.

The codebase's own norm is documented against this: components/charts/constants.py:255 says QUALITY_INDEX_MAX is 'Fixed so a model keeps the same vertical position ... whatever the filter', components/charts/local_scatter.py:146 uses `range=[0, QUALITY_INDEX_MAX]`, and quadrant.py:36-39 already pins bubble size to BUBBLE_PRICE_REF for exactly this reason — but quadrant.py:55 still does `y_max = plot_df["quality"].max() * 1.15`. tests/test_pareto_chart.py:204 asserts bubble-size invariance under filtering; nothing asserts threshold or y-range invariance.

Best counter-argument I could find, which I judge insufficient: median crosshairs in a quadrant chart are conventionally relative to what is plotted. But the y-axis-range half has no such defence (it directly contradicts the stated invariant and local_scatter's implementation), and a quality-only filter silently moving the SPEED threshold is not something the convention predicts.

title: Radar axis ceilings are uncalibrated against the population: Speed is dead, Context caps at 50%, Latency saturates
evidence:
Ran `./ai-frontier/bin/python` over the live cache (data/raw/aa_models.csv, 148 rows) comparing each RADAR_* constant to the actual population:

  AXIS            const   pop-max   pop-max/const   pop-median/const
  Intelligence       70      63.0         0.901            0.404
  Speed            2500    1559.9         0.624            0.041
  Context(k)       2000    1000.0         0.500            0.131
  Price              50      40.0         0.800            0.019
  Latency            30      101.9         3.396            0.039

- Speed: 89.2% of all 148 models fall inside the innermost 10% of the radius; 98.6% inside 20%. No model in the catalog reaches 62% of RADAR_SPEED_MAX.
- Context: RADAR_CONTEXT_K_MAX=2000 but the largest context in the data is '1m' = 1000k, so the Context spoke can never exceed exactly 0.5. Every one of the 52 '1m' models plots at exactly 0.500.
- Latency: RADAR_LATENCY_MAX=30s but pop max is 101.9s. 10 of 148 models have latency >= 30s and all clamp to 0 (radar.py:91).

The shipped figure proves it is live, not hypothetical — docs/figures/radar.json:
  Claude Opus 5 (Max Effort) -> Speed 0.021, Context 0.500, Latency 0.000
  Claude Opus 5 (Xhigh)      -> Speed 0.020, Context 0.500, Latency 0.419
  Kimi K2.7 Code             -> Speed 0.119, Context 0.128, Latency 0.971
  GPT-5.6 Luna (xhigh)       -> Speed 0.064, Context 0.500, Latency 0.000
The Compare tab's default 5 (static_helpers.compute_diverse5) deliberately includes a 'fastest model' pick — Kimi K2.7 Code at 298 tok/s — and it renders at 11.9% vs Claude Opus 5's 2.1%. Both look like the centre of the plot.

GPT-5.6 Luna (xhigh) has latency 30.84s and GPT-5.6 Terra (max) has 101.87s; both hover as 'Latency: 0%'. No test asserts these constants against the data (grep RADAR over tests/ returns nothing), and git log on constants.py shows they were never recalibrated.
user_impact: A user opens Compare to answer 'is model A faster than model B'. All five default polygons collapse onto the Speed spoke at 2-12% of the radius, so the chart shows no visible difference between a 52 tok/s model and a 298 tok/s model — the axis is unusable for its only purpose. The Context spoke can never fill past halfway even for the largest window in the catalog, so a 1M-token model reads as 'mediocre context'. And a model with 32s TTFT is drawn identically to one with 102s. The title asserts 'normalized 0-100 across all models', which is false: the maxima are hand-picked round numbers no model reaches (Speed/Context) or that a tenth of the catalog blows past (Latency).
suggested_fix: Derive the ceilings once from the FULL unfiltered catalog at load time (e.g. a p99 or max of df.speed, ctx_k, price, latency), cache them as module constants so they stay filter-independent — that preserves the shape-stability the comment at radar.py:56-61 was protecting — and either use a log or rank transform for Speed/Latency (both are heavy-tailed) or clamp at p95 and mark clamped spokes visually. At minimum set RADAR_SPEED_MAX≈1600, RADAR_CONTEXT_K_MAX≈1000, RADAR_LATENCY_MAX≈105 and change the subtitle to state the actual reference values.
verify_reasoning: Tried to refute by checking for a rescaling step in the JS path and by re-deriving the population stats myself. Both failed to kill it. Ran `./ai-frontier/bin/python` over `data/ingest.load_cached()` (148 rows): speed max 1559.89 (0.624 of RADAR_SPEED_MAX=2500), median 103.17; context max via radar._context_k = 1000.0 (exactly 0.500 of RADAR_CONTEXT_K_MAX=2000), with 52 rows at exactly 1000; latency max 101.87 vs RADAR_LATENCY_MAX=30 with 10 rows >= 30; quality max 63.05 of QUALITY_INDEX_MAX=70; price max 40.0 of 50. 132/148 (89.2%) have speed < 250, i.e. inside the innermost 10% of the radius. Line citations are exact: constants.py:260 is `RADAR_SPEED_MAX = 2500.0`. The shipped docs/figures/radar.json independently confirms it is live, not hypothetical: r arrays are Speed 0.021/0.024/0.119/0.064/0.020 and Context 0.500 for four of the five default models. The JS path does not rescale — docs/app.js:443 `renderJsonFig` is a bare `Plotly.react(divId, figObj.data, figObj.layout, ...)`, so the Python r values ship verbatim. Verified the 'fastest model' default pick is real: static_helpers.compute_diverse5:45-47 picks max speed with quality>=40, which resolves to Kimi K2.7 Code at 298.11 tok/s — rendered at 0.119 against Claude Opus 5's 0.021. Verified the latency clamp victims: GPT-5.6 Luna (xhigh) 30.84s and GPT-5.6 Terra (max) 101.87s both clamp to 0 at radar.py:97 and both hover 'Latency: 0%'. grep for RADAR/radar across tests/ returns only a figure-id string in tests/test_build_static.py:35 — no constant is asserted against the data. Keeping HIGH: the latency clamp destroys real differences among exactly the flagship max-effort configs users open Compare to compare, and the title at radar.py:126 asserts 'normalized 0-100 across all models', which the fixed hand-picked ceilings make false in both directions.

title: Compare tab silently destroys the user's model selection whenever any global filter changes
evidence:
app.py:1153-1156:
    if triggered in ("filter-provider", "filter-quality", "model-search"):
        capped = _compute_diverse5(filtered)
    else:
        capped = (selected_models or [])[:5]
The `selected_models` Input is discarded unconditionally — it is not pruned, it is thrown away and replaced by an auto-picked set.

End-to-end browser proof (live Dash server on :8051, DEBUG=true so no scrapers): on ?tab=compare I deselected the 5 defaults and built a deliberate 3-model comparison. `#radar-chart` traces read exactly ["Mistral Medium 3.5", "Grok 4.5 (high)", "Llama 4 Maverick"], value-count "3 selected". I then clicked the "Top 25%" preset in the global filter bar (a single click on an unrelated control). Immediately after: radar traces = ["Claude Opus 5 (Adaptive Reas…", "DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (Reas…", "Kimi K2.7 Code", "GPT-5.6 Luna (xhigh)", "Claude Opus 5 (Adaptive Reas…"], value-count "5 selected".

This is not legitimate pruning. The preset applies quality >= _P75 = 42.1, and `Grok 4.5 (high)` has quality 55.76 (verified: `d.loc['Grok 4.5 (high)','quality']` = 55.76 >= 42.1 -> True). It still satisfied the new filter and was dropped anyway.

Direct callback invocation reproduces it for all three trigger ids — with picks=['Claude Opus 5 (Adaptive Reasoning, Max Effort)','GPT-5.6 Luna (xhigh)','Gemini 3.5 Pro'], calling update_compare with ctx.triggered_id='model-search' and search='gpt' returned value=['GPT-5.6 Sol (max)','GPT-5.6 Luna (max)','GPT-5.6 Luna (xhigh)','GPT-5.6 Terra (max)','GPT-5.6 Sol (xhigh)'] (picks preserved: False); with triggered_id='filter-quality' and min_quality=20 it returned the _DIVERSE5 default (picks preserved: False). Clearing the search afterwards does NOT restore the picks — it recomputes diverse5 on the full frame again, so there is no undo.
user_impact: A user assembles the exact 3-5 model comparison they care about on the Compare tab — the one tab whose entire purpose is a curated selection. They then touch the always-visible global filter bar (type in SEARCH, change MIN SCORE, pick a provider, or click a preset) to narrow the field, which is the natural next step. Their selection is silently replaced by an algorithmic pick. Nothing warns them, and clearing the filter does not bring it back — the selection must be rebuilt by hand from a 148-entry dropdown.
suggested_fix: Prune rather than reset: keep the models the user chose that still satisfy the new filter, and only fall back to _compute_diverse5(filtered) when the intersection is empty. e.g. `kept = [m for m in (selected_models or []) if m in set(filtered['model'])]; capped = kept[:5] or _compute_diverse5(filtered)`. If a reset is genuinely wanted, surface it (a "selection reset by filter" note next to the dropdown) instead of doing it silently.
verify_reasoning: Tried to refute by (a) looking for a prune/restore path and (b) checking whether the reset is reachable only when the selection becomes invalid. Neither holds. grep for Output("radar-model-select","value") returns only update_compare (app.py:1140-1158) and add_to_compare (app.py:1332-1345) — nothing restores a prior selection, and there is no url-sync of the compare picks. I re-ran the callback directly with a fake ctx (dash 4.0.0 leaves the undecorated function bound in the module namespace, verified via inspect.signature): picks=['Mistral Medium 3.5','Grok 4.5 (high)','Llama 4 Maverick'] with triggered_id='filter-quality', min_quality=_P75=42.1 returned the _DIVERSE5 default; 'model-search'/'gpt' returned five GPT models; 'filter-provider'/['Anthropic'] returned five Claude models. Grok 4.5 (high) quality is 55.76 >= 42.1, i.e. it still passed the new filter and was still discarded, so this is not pruning. Control: triggered_id='radar-model-select' with the same picks returned them unchanged, so the reset is specifically the three global-filter triggers. This is NOT Dash-only — static_api.py:248-254 carries the identical `if triggered in ("filter-provider","filter-quality","model-search"): capped = compute_diverse5(f)` branch, and docs/app.js:685 calls refreshCompare("filter-provider") on every global-filter change, so the live GitHub Pages site does the same thing. Severity high stands.

title: Radar axes are normalized against fixed constants far outside the data range, collapsing Speed and flattening Latency, while the caption claims normalization against the dataset best
evidence:
radar.py:62-66 normalizes each axis against a fixed constant (q_max=QUALITY_INDEX_MAX, s_max=RADAR_SPEED_MAX, p_max=RADAR_PRICE_MAX, l_max=RADAR_LATENCY_MAX, c_max=RADAR_CONTEXT_K_MAX), defined at constants.py:255,260-263. app.py:509-510 tells the user these are "all normalized to 0–100% relative to the best model in the full dataset."

Measured constants vs the 148-row frame:
  quality max=  63.05   QUALITY_INDEX_MAX  = 70.0
  speed   max=1559.89   RADAR_SPEED_MAX    = 2500.0   (median speed 103.2)
  price   max=  40.00   RADAR_PRICE_MAX    = 50.0
  latency max= 101.87   RADAR_LATENCY_MAX  = 30.0     <- constant is 3.4x too small
  ctx (k) max=1000.00   RADAR_CONTEXT_K_MAX= 2000.0

No axis reaches 100% at the dataset best, contradicting the caption:
  Intelligence  best Claude Opus 5 (63.05)     -> renders  90.1%
  Speed         best Celeris-1 (1559.9)        -> renders  62.4%
  Context       best Claude Opus 5 (1000k)     -> renders  50.0%

Speed axis is functionally dead — render-% histogram across all 148 models: 0-5%:91, 5-10%:41, 10-25%:14, 25-50%:1, 50-100%:1. 132/148 models render below 10%. The default Compare selection renders Speed at 2%, 2%, 12%, 6%, 2%.

Latency axis silently flattens the worst performers: 10/148 models have TTFT >= 30s and all clamp to a flat 0% (radar.py:91 `min(1.0, max(0.0, v))`). GPT-5.6 Terra (max) at 101.87s, Claude Sonnet 5 (Max Effort) at 93.81s, Reka Flash 3 at 91.05s, GPT-5.6 Sol (max) at 76.53s and 6 others are all drawn identically. Verified there are currently 0 models with missing latency, so the conflation today is worst-vs-worst, not worst-vs-unknown.
user_impact: A user opens Compare to answer "which of these 5 models is fastest?" — the chart's stated purpose. Four of the five default models sit at 2-6% on the Speed spoke, visually collapsed onto the polar origin and indistinguishable, even though their real throughputs differ several-fold. On Latency, a model with 30s TTFT and one with 102s TTFT draw the same zero-length spoke. The hover tooltip reports these as percentages, so the user reads "Intelligence: 90%" for the single best model in the dataset and reasonably infers something scores higher.
suggested_fix: Derive each axis ceiling from the full unfiltered dataset once at import (the property the caption already promises) rather than from hand-set constants — e.g. `s_max = FULL_DF['speed'].max()`, `l_max = FULL_DF['latency'].max()`. That keeps the shape stable across filter state (the reason the constants were introduced) while making the axes span the real data. If constants must stay, correct RADAR_LATENCY_MAX to >= the observed max and rewrite the app.py:509 caption to state the actual reference values.
verify_reasoning: Every number reproduced by executing build_radar against the live 148-row frame. Constants (components/charts/constants.py:255,260-263) vs data: quality max 63.05 vs QUALITY_INDEX_MAX 70.0; speed max 1559.89 vs RADAR_SPEED_MAX 2500.0 (median 103.2); price max 40.00 vs 50.0; latency max 101.87 vs RADAR_LATENCY_MAX 30.0; context max 1000k vs 2000.0. build_radar(df,_DIVERSE5) trace radii, read straight off the figure: Claude Opus 5 [90.1, 2.1, 60.0, 50.0, 0.0], DeepSeek V4 Flash [74.0, 2.4, 99.7, 50.0, 98.2], Kimi K2.7 Code [61.5, 11.9, 94.4, 12.8, 97.1], GPT-5.6 Luna (xhigh) [71.5, 6.4, 98.1, 50.0, 0.0], Claude Opus 5 xhigh [89.3, 2.0, 60.0, 50.0, 41.9] — so the dataset's single best model renders Intelligence at 90.1%, not 100%, directly contradicting app.py:510 'relative to the best model in the full dataset'. numpy histogram of speed render-% over all 148 rows = [91, 41, 14, 1, 1] for bins 0-5/5-10/10-25/25-50/50-100, i.e. 132/148 under 10% — the speed spoke is functionally dead. 10 models have TTFT >= 30s (max 101.87s, GPT-5.6 Terra) and I confirmed 0 NaN and 0 non-positive latencies, so the clamp at radar.py:91 collapses ten genuinely different models onto an identical 0% spoke rather than conflating with unknowns. Refutation attempts that failed: the in-file comment (radar.py:56-61) justifies fixed ceilings for filter-stability, but that does not make the caption true, and the ceilings could be set from the full frame and still be stable. Scope note: radar.py and constants.py are both vendored inside docs/pybundle.zip with the same 2500.0/30.0 values, so the collapsed axes ship to the public site; only the false caption is Dash-only (no such text in docs/index.html). Severity high stands.

title: ?tab=<unknown> in a shared URL blanks the entire public dashboard
evidence: `applyUrlState` (app.js:750-762) ends with `if (u.get("tab")) switchTab(u.get("tab"));` — no validation. `switchTab` (159-172) loops TABS and sets `display = t.id === id ? "block" : "none"`, so an id matching nothing hides every panel and selects no tab button. Loaded http://127.0.0.1:8099/index.html?tab=performance in a browser against docs/: {stateTab:"performance", selectedTabs:[], visiblePanels:[], visibleTabControlRows:[], tabPanelsHeight:0}. app.py:883-887 defines `_VALID_TABS` and falls back to "overview", with a comment stating this exact bug ('a shared ?tab=image link silently reset to Overview') was already fixed once — on the Dash side only.

title: "Updated just now" is stamped even when the scrape that feeds 7 of 10 tabs failed — proven on run 31558618824
evidence:
The badge's only source is `generated_iso`, set to `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` at **build** time (build_static.py:82,98) and rendered verbatim by `renderFreshness()` (docs/app.js:424-431: `el.textContent = "Updated " + relativeTime(iso)`). Nothing in the manifest records per-dataset scrape success. The change guard (refresh.yml:44-52) fires if ANY file under data/raw/ moved, and the rebuild+commit+push steps (refresh.yml:58-69) run on that single boolean — the "Report scrape failures" step that reddens the run is deliberately LAST (refresh.yml:73-77), i.e. after the lie is already published.

PROVEN, not hypothetical. `gh run view 31558618824 --log` (2026-08-12T02:59Z):
  [scraper] Unexpected API response structure          <- hosted LLM scrape FAILED
  [local_scraper] No valid open-weight model rows parsed <- local scrape FAILED
  [image_scraper] Saved 148 image models                 <- only image succeeded
  data guard OK
  Data-only rebuild complete -> .../docs
  [main ff0ef24] data: hourly AA refresh (2026-08-12T02:59Z)
     583ff27..ff0ef24  main -> main                      <- PUSHED
  ##[error]hosted local served from cache

`gh api .../commits/ff0ef24` -> files changed: data/raw/aa_image_models.csv, docs/figures/image_faceted.json, docs/figures/manifest.json, docs/pybundle.zip. **aa_models.csv is not in that list.** The manifest at that commit reads `generated_iso = 2026-08-12T02:59:44.630413+00:00`.

`gh api "...commits?path=data/raw/aa_models.csv"` shows aa_models.csv last actually changed at 2026-08-11T21:47:38Z and not again until 2026-08-12T12:02:41Z. aa_local_models.csv last changed 2026-08-11T07:41:41Z.

So at 02:59:45Z the live site said "Updated just now" while the LLM catalogue was 5 h 12 m old (and its endpoint was down) and the Run Local catalogue was 19 h 18 m old (same endpoint down). Aggravating factor: data/scraper.py:39-42 and data/local_scraper.py:30-33 hit the *identical* URL, so those two always fail together, while the image scraper (a different URL, an ELO arena that churns constantly) changes almost every hour — 34 of the last 40 bot commits touched aa_image_models.csv. The one dataset that reliably bumps the badge is the one least coupled to the other two.
user_impact: A visitor comparing GPT/Claude/Gemini prices reads "Updated just now" in the header and trusts the numbers as current. During an AA outage of the host-models endpoint the LLM and Run Local tabs are served from a cache that can be many hours or (as with the 29-day image outage this workflow was written to prevent) many days old, while the badge keeps resetting to "just now" on the strength of an unrelated image-ELO refresh. The run turns red in the Actions tab, but nothing on the page tells the visitor.
suggested_fix: Stop deriving freshness from build time. Have each scraper write its own `{dataset: {ok: bool, fetched_at: iso, rows: n}}` record, fold all three into manifest.json, and have renderFreshness() show the OLDEST successful fetch time — plus an explicit warning chip ("LLM data 5 h old — upstream failing") whenever any dataset's `ok` is false or its `fetched_at` is older than ~3 h. As a stopgap, gate the manifest's generated_iso bump on `steps.scrape.outputs.failed == ''` so a partial refresh cannot reset the clock.
verify_reasoning:
Tried to refute by finding a second freshness surface or a per-dataset status field. There is none: `grep -n "generated\|coverage" docs/app.js` returns exactly two hits (app.js:188 `window.AF.generatedIso = m.generated_iso`, app.js:190 renderCoverageNote), and renderFreshness (docs/app.js:424-431) prints `"Updated " + relativeTime(iso)` from that single build-time value written at build_static.py:82,98. The manifest keys (build_static.py:83-99) carry no per-dataset scrape status.

Independently re-derived the incident. `gh run view 31558618824` shows Scrape/Change guard/Sanity check/Rebuild/Commit+push all green and only the LAST step 'Report scrape failures' red, with annotations 'no fresh data for: hosted local (served cache instead)' — i.e. the push happened before the run went red, exactly as refresh.yml:58-77 orders it. `gh api repos/.../commits/ff0ef24` -> files = aa_image_models.csv, image_faceted.json, manifest.json, pybundle.zip; aa_models.csv absent. `gh api .../contents/docs/figures/manifest.json?ref=ff0ef24` -> generated_iso = 2026-08-12T02:59:44.630413+00:00. Commit history for aa_models.csv: previous real change 2026-08-11T21:47:38Z, next 2026-08-12T12:02:41Z (so 5 h 12 m stale at publish); aa_local_models.csv previous change 2026-08-11T07:41:41Z (19 h 18 m stale). Badge would have read 'just now'.

Also confirmed both aggravators: data/scraper.py:39-42 and data/local_scraper.py:30-33 hold the byte-identical URL (host-models/performance?prompt_length=1000), so they always fail together; and since 2026-08-11 aa_image_models.csv changed in 30 commits vs 6 for aa_models.csv and 5 for aa_local_models.csv — the image ELO scrape is what keeps resetting the clock.

Severity lowered to high: the displayed numbers are real (just hours old) and the maintainer does get a red run, so this is misleading-UI rather than data corruption.

title: An AA field rename outside the 3 hard-fail keys silently publishes an all-zero column; the row-count guard cannot see it and the workflow stays green
evidence:
Every field is read with `.get(...) or <default>`, so a rename degrades to a default instead of raising. data/scraper.py:112-114:
    ts = hm.get("timescaleData") or {}
    speed   = ts.get("median_output_speed") or 0
    latency = ts.get("median_time_to_first_chunk") or 0

I executed `_parse_api_response` against a 60-record synthetic payload with fields renamed one at a time (./ai-frontier/bin/python, plotly 6.5.2):
  baseline                                  rows=60 df=60 speed_nonzero=60 provider=['Acme'] ctx=['128k']
  timescaleData -> perfData                 rows=60 df=60 speed_nonzero=0 lat_nonzero=0     <- ALL ZERO, no error
  model_creators -> creator                 rows=60 df=60 provider=['']                     <- every provider blank
  context_window_formatted+tokens dropped   rows=60 df=60 ctx=['0']                          <- every context '0'
  intelligence_index -> aa_index            KeyError -> caught -> exit 1                     <- loud (correct)
  all three price keys renamed               DF EMPTY -> exit 1                              <- loud (correct)

Only the name/score/price keys fail loudly. Everything else becomes a silent constant. `data_guard.py` cannot catch it: `_row_count` (data_guard.py:39-42) parses the CSV and returns `len(df)` — nothing else. I verified on the real cache that zeroing speed leaves the row count identical at 148, so `check()` (data_guard.py:64-92) returns no problems and the run publishes.

Downstream, with speed/latency zeroed on the real 148-row cache:
  build_quadrant        -> traces=0, annotations=0   (quadrant.py:22-31 filters speed>0 then `return go.Figure()`)
  build_rankings(speed) -> traces=0, annotation 'No models match these filters'
  pareto / treemap / provider_leaderboard / value_leaders / cost_calc -> render normally
So the site looks ~90% healthy: one panel is blank with no explanation, one blames the user's filters, and every remaining chart silently drops speed from its tooltips.
user_impact: The day Artificial Analysis renames `timescaleData` (they already renamed `tag.label` -> `tag.displayName`, see image_scraper.py:16-18), the hourly bot publishes 148 models with speed=0 and latency=0, marks the run green, and stamps "Updated just now". The Speed vs Quality quadrant goes completely blank with no message, and the speed leaderboard tells the user "No models match these filters" when their filters are fine. Nobody is alerted; the only symptom is a blank panel.
suggested_fix: Add a schema assertion to each scraper: after parsing, require that the share of rows with a usable value in each critical column (speed, latency, provider, context) exceeds a floor (e.g. 80%), and return False otherwise so the existing `|| failed=` guard fires. Extend data_guard.py beyond `_row_count` to a per-column health check on the same CSVs (non-null fraction, non-zero fraction, distinct-provider count) compared against HEAD. Separately, make build_quadrant return a figure with an explicit "speed data unavailable" annotation instead of a bare `go.Figure()`, and stop build_rankings blaming the filters when the metric column itself is dead.
verify_reasoning:
Tried to refute by looking for a schema guard in the scraper, in load_from_raw, or in data_guard. None exists. Reproduced the finder's table exactly with ./ai-frontier/bin/python on a 60-record synthetic payload through data.scraper._parse_api_response + data.ingest.load_from_raw:
  baseline                       rows=60 df=60 speed_nonzero=60 providers=['Acme'] ctx=['128k']
  timescaleData -> perfData      rows=60 df=60 speed_nonzero=0 lat_nonzero=0   (silent)
  median_output_speed renamed    rows=60 df=60 speed_nonzero=0 lat_nonzero=60  (silent)
  model_creators -> creator      rows=60 df=60 providers=['']                  (silent)
  context window keys dropped    rows=60 df=60 ctx=['0']                        (silent)
  intelligence_index -> aa_index rows=0 -> scrape_and_save returns False (loud, exit 1)
  all 3 price keys renamed       rows=0 -> loud, exit 1
So only the score/price/name keys fail loudly, exactly as claimed (the mechanism for the score rename is the skipped["no_score"] path at scraper.py:70-72, not a KeyError as the finder wrote — same loud outcome).

Reproduced the downstream on the real 148-row cache with speed/latency zeroed:

  build_rankings(speed) traces=0 annotation 'No models match these filters'

Baseline for contrast: quadrant traces=11, rankings(speed) traces=2.

Checked reachability rather than assuming it: the blank quadrant is user-reachable on the public site via the Overview x-axis radio (docs/index.html:76 value="speed" -> docs/app.js:667/814 -> static_api.py:223 `build_quadrant(f) if xaxis == "speed"`). data_guard cannot see it — _row_count (data_guard.py:39-42) returns only len(df), which is unchanged.

title: Unchecking every provider on the Agent Stack tab is silently identical to checking "All"
evidence:
app.py:1041-1048 and static_api.py:388-395 deliberately distinguish the two states — `if mode == 'local': providers = None` / `elif not selected: providers = []` / `elif '__all__' in selected: providers = None` — so `[]` is meant to be "no providers". But `select_stack` at stack_recommender.py:425 tests `if providers:`, and an empty list is falsy, so no filter is applied. Its own docstring (line 420) says "None = all".
Executed:
  update_recommend([], 'api', None, 32, 1, 'Q4')  vs  update_recommend(['__all__'], 'api', None, 32, 1, 'Q4')
  -> cards_html identical: True  (both 32478 chars)
  providers appearing in the 'nothing checked' output: ['Alibaba', 'Anthropic', 'DeepSeek', 'MiniMax', 'OpenAI']
  update_recommend(['Anthropic'], ...) differs, confirming the filter works when non-empty.
user_impact: A user who wants to see what an all-open-weights stack looks like unchecks Anthropic, Google and OpenAI (the three defaults). The recommendation cards come back showing Anthropic, OpenAI, Alibaba and DeepSeek models — exactly the providers they just excluded — with nothing indicating the selection was ignored. They then act on a stack recommendation built from a provider set they explicitly rejected.
suggested_fix: Make the empty case explicit at stack_recommender.py:425: `if providers is not None: api_pool = api_pool[api_pool['provider'].isin(providers)]`, and have `_tier_card` render the existing "No models match" state when the pool is empty. The three call sites already pass `None` for "all", so this needs no caller change.
verify_reasoning: Read components/stack_recommender.py:424-426 — `api_pool = df.copy()` then `if providers:` — and confirmed the docstring at line 419 says 'None = all', so `[]` is intended to be distinct. Ran the comparison myself: `update_recommend([], 'api', None, 32, 1, 'Q4')` and `update_recommend(['__all__'], 'api', None, 32, 1, 'Q4')` return byte-identical cards_html (32478 chars each), while `update_recommend(['Anthropic'], …)` differs — so the filter works when non-empty and is simply skipped when empty. Scanned the 'nothing checked' HTML for provider names: Alibaba, Anthropic, DeepSeek, MiniMax, OpenAI all present. Checked reachability in the actual UI rather than assuming it: docs/index.html:219-237 are seven independent checkboxes (Anthropic/Google/OpenAI pre-checked, plus a separate '__all__' box), so unchecking the three defaults yields exactly `[]` — there is no 'at least one' constraint anywhere. app.py:1041-1048 has the identical resolve logic, so both renderings. Severity high stands: a user's explicit exclusion is silently inverted into 'show everything', and the excluded providers are what gets recommended.

title: Treemap colour ramp gets DARKER as intelligence rises over its first 30%, inverting the encoding for 13 of 33 providers
evidence:
The colorscale stops are [0.0 '#243056'], [0.3 '#16213e'], [0.55 '#0f3460'], [0.75 '#1a5276'], [0.9 '#00909e'], [1.0 '#00d4ff'] with cmin=0, cmax=QUALITY_INDEX_MAX=70. Relative luminance of the stops:
  score  0.0  #243056  L=0.0316
  score 21.0  #16213e  L=0.0161   <-- DARKER than score 0
  score 38.5  #0f3460  L=0.0340
  score 52.5  #1a5276  L=0.0756
  score 63.0  #00909e  L=0.2242
  score 70.0  #00d4ff  L=0.5431
Luminance is non-monotonic: it falls from score 0 to score 21, then rises. This holds for the stops themselves, independent of how Plotly interpolates.

Computed tile colours for the live 33-provider frame (values/colors read straight off the returned go.Treemap; I verified marker.colors == groupby mean exactly, max |diff| = 0.0, and values == model_count exactly):
  Reka AI     avg  3.71  #222d52  L*=19.40
  Meta        avg  9.24  #1e294b  L*=17.47
  NVIDIA      avg 12.84  #1b2747  L*=16.20
  Arcee AI    avg 18.37  #182341  L*=14.22
  Inception   avg 21.90  #162240  L*=13.69   <-- darkest tile on the chart
  Alibaba     avg 25.96  #142648  L*=15.61
  Google      avg 28.76  #13294d  L*=16.94
13 of 33 providers fall on the inverted 0-21 segment; 112 provider pairs render with the lower-scoring one lighter.
Magnitudes: Reka AI (3.71) vs Inception (21.90) = dE76 6.77 with Reka LIGHTER. Meta (9.24) vs Google (28.76) = dE76 2.73 with Meta LIGHTER — a 19.5-point real gap read backwards. By contrast Mistral (15.02) vs Alibaba (25.96) is dE76 1.99, below a just-noticeable difference, for an 11-point real gap. The inversion signal is stronger than the true signal in the same region.

This ships: docs/figures/treemap.json carries the identical colorscale and cmin/cmax. The code comment at treemap.py:43-49 explicitly claims this exact failure ('could go DARKER as its average quality rose, inverting the encoding') was fixed — the autoscaling half was fixed, the ramp itself was not.
user_impact: On the Provider Landscape treemap the subtitle promises 'color = avg intelligence' and the colorbar runs dark-to-cyan, so a reader reads brighter as smarter. Meta's tile (avg intelligence 9.2) is visibly lighter than Google's (avg 28.8) and than Inception's (avg 21.9), so the reader concludes Meta's catalogue is stronger than Google's when it is roughly a third as strong. Every provider below ~21 average — 13 of 33, including Meta, NVIDIA, Mistral, Amazon, Cohere, IBM, Microsoft — is ranked backwards against its neighbours.
suggested_fix: Replace the ramp with one monotonic in lightness across all six stops — e.g. drop the '#243056' stop and start the scale at the darkest colour (#16213e at 0.0), or reorder to #101828 -> #16213e -> #0f3460 -> #1a5276 -> #00909e -> #00d4ff and verify. Add a test that walks the colorscale at 0.01 increments, converts each interpolated colour to relative luminance, and asserts the sequence is non-decreasing.
verify_reasoning:
Tried to refute by (a) checking whether Plotly's interpolation smooths the inversion away and (b) checking whether the magnitudes are actually perceptible. (a) fails, (b) partly succeeds — enough to cut the severity, not the finding.

Walked the colorscale from components/charts/treemap.py:51-58 at 0.005 steps, interpolating linearly in RGB (which is what Plotly does), and converting to WCAG relative luminance: 60 consecutive negative steps, spanning t=0.0 to t=0.30 exactly, with the global minimum at t=0.30 (score 21.0). Stop luminances reproduce the finder's table to 4 dp: 0.0316, 0.0161, 0.0340, 0.0756, 0.2242, 0.5431. So the ramp is monotonically DARKENING over the bottom 30% of its domain.

Read values/colors off the returned go.Treemap for the live frame: marker.colors == groupby('provider')['quality'].mean() with max |diff| = 0.0, values == model count exactly. 32 providers (finder said 33 — minor error; C(32,2)=496 pairs). 13 providers fall at or below score 21, and 112 of 496 pairs render the higher-scoring provider darker — 112 matches the finder exactly. Recomputed CIELAB dE76 independently: Reka AI (3.71) vs Inception (21.90) = 6.77 with Reka lighter; Meta (9.24) vs Google (28.76) = 2.73 with Meta lighter; Mistral (15.02) vs Alibaba (25.96) = 1.99. All three match to 2 dp. Hex tiles match too (#222d52, #1e294b, #1b2747, #162240, #142648, #13294d). docs/figures/treemap.json carries the identical colorscale with cmin 0.0 / cmax 70.0, so it ships.

Severity downgraded from high to medium: the inversion is objectively real and the title does promise 'color = avg intelligence', but the whole affected band is a near-flat dark navy — Meta vs Google is dE 2.73, right at the just-noticeable threshold, so 'Meta's tile is visibly lighter than Google's' overstates it. Only the widest pair (Reka vs Inception, dE 6.77) is clearly readable backwards. The practical defect is 'the bottom 30% of the ramp carries almost no discriminable signal, and what little it carries points the wrong way'.

Computed diameters on the 95 plotted (deduped) models:
  $0.00-$0.50   n=32   25.76 .. 25.96 px
  $0.50-$1.00   n=21   25.53 .. 25.76 px
  $1.00-$2.00   n=12   25.03 .. 25.42 px
  $2.00-$5.00   n=10   23.86 .. 25.02 px
  $5.00-$10.00  n=12   20.77 .. 23.45 px
  $10.00-$20.00 n= 4   19.02 .. 20.44 px
  >= $20.00     n= 4    7.00 ..  7.00 px

title: data_guard validates row counts only, so the price regression that actually happened sailed through with the row count going UP
evidence:
`check()` computes `drop_pct = (before - now)/before*100` from `_row_count()` (data_guard.py:39-42, `len(pd.read_csv(...))`) and compares nothing else — no value ranges, no distribution, no column presence, no unit sanity.

The regression it was supposed to prevent is exactly the class it cannot see. On the 2026-05-06 price-basis flip (see `price-blend-inverted`), data/raw/history/aa_models_2026-04-16.csv -> aa_models_2026-05-06.csv went 255 -> 283 rows, i.e. +11.0%. Every price roughly doubled while the guard's only metric moved in the *safe* direction. Running the guard today: `./ai-frontier/bin/python data_guard.py` -> "data guard OK", 148 / 97 / 148 rows, +0 each — it is green on data whose entire price column is ~1.9x AA's.

The threshold itself is not the problem: across all 90 archived snapshots only two day-over-day steps ever exceeded 20% (2026-03-06->03-07 68.1%, the host-level poisoned snapshot; 2026-07-24->07-25 53.2%, the real AA pruning). Every other step is <=5.0%. So the 20% relative rule does fire on genuine row loss — it is dimensionally blind, not loose.

Second gap: the guard exists only in .github/workflows/refresh.yml:55-57. app.py:54-56 starts all three scrapers in-process on every Dash boot, and `data.ingest.save_cache` (ingest.py:102-111) overwrites data/raw/aa_models.csv AND writes data/raw/history/aa_models_<today>.csv `if not snap_path.exists()` — permanently freezing that day's archival record — with no guard on that path at all.
user_impact: Any upstream change that alters values without changing row counts (a renamed/removed field falling through to a different formula, a unit change from per-1M to per-1k tokens, a rescaled intelligence index) is published to GitHub Pages with a green CI run and no warning. This has already happened once and stayed live for 99 days. Additionally, a developer who runs `python app.py` on a day the bot has not yet snapshotted writes that day's permanent history row from their own unguarded scrape.
suggested_fix: Extend data_guard.py beyond row counts: for each numeric column compare the current median against HEAD's and fail on a shift beyond a band (e.g. >25%), assert the columns present at HEAD still exist, and assert the invariant price_in <= price <= price_out. Also invoke the guard from `data.scraper.scrape_and_save` before `save_cache`, so the local/in-process write path is protected too.
verify_reasoning:
I read data_guard.py end to end and ran it. check() (data_guard.py:62-91) computes only drop_pct from _row_count() (:38-41, len(pd.read_csv(...))) plus the MIN_ROWS=50 floor. There is no value, distribution, column-presence or unit check anywhere in the file — I confirmed by reading, not inference.

Ran it: `./ai-frontier/bin/python data_guard.py` -> 148/97/148 rows, +0 each, "data guard OK", exit 0 — green on the exact data I independently proved is ~1.9x AA's published price in the finding above.

The row counts across the price flip are as stated: data/raw/history/aa_models_2026-04-16.csv = 255 rows, aa_models_2026-05-06.csv = 283 rows, i.e. +11.0%, moving in the safe direction while every price roughly doubled.

Threshold sanity claim also holds: scanning all 90 archived snapshots, only three day-over-day steps exceed 20% (2026-02-25->03-06 -594% growth, 2026-03-06->03-07 68.1% drop, 2026-07-24->07-25 53.2% drop). The finder missed the first (a growth step, which the guard ignores by design) but the substance — the 20% rule is dimensionally blind, not loose — is right.

Call-site claim verified by grep: the only non-test invocation is .github/workflows/refresh.yml:57. app.py:52-55 starts start_background_scraper / start_background_image_scraper / start_background_local_scraper on boot, and data/ingest.py:102-111 save_cache() writes CACHE_PATH then `if not snap_path.exists()` writes data/raw/history/aa_models_<today>.csv — permanently freezing that day's archive — with no guard on that path.

Downgrading high -> medium: this is a missing check giving false assurance, not a wrong value shipped to users. Its only demonstrated consequence is the price-blend finding, which I have already scored separately; double-counting the same incident at high in both places overstates it.

title: VRAM requirement has no context-length / KV-cache term at all, despite the docstrings claiming it does — "fits" verdicts are unreachable at the advertised context
evidence:
`calc_vram_gb(params_b, quant) -> params_b * QUANT_BYTES[quant] * _OVERHEAD` (line 485). Verified signature has only two args: `('params_b','quant')`. `context_k` is carried in every catalog row but is never read by `get_local_df` (lines 548-572) — I confirmed models with `context_k` 8 / 128 / 1000 / 10000 all get vram_req computed the same way. Yet line 9 states "VRAM formula: params_b × bytes_per_weight × OVERHEAD_FACTOR" and lines 35-36 label `_OVERHEAD = 1.18` as the "KV-cache + activation overhead multiplier".

Computed true fp16 KV cache from published architectures (layers × kv_heads × head_dim × 2 × 2 bytes × tokens):
  Llama 3.1 8B (32L, 8 KV heads, 128 dim): weights Q4 = 4.74 GB; KV @128k = 17.18 GB -> 78.4% of true footprint unaccounted; @32k = 4.29 GB -> 47.5% unaccounted.
  Qwen3 32B (64L, 8, 128): weights Q4 = 19.35 GB; KV @128k = 34.36 GB -> 64.0% unaccounted.
  Llama 3.3 70B (80L, 8, 128): weights Q4 = 41.30 GB; KV @128k = 42.95 GB -> 51.0% unaccounted.

Concrete UI case: on an RTX 5080 (16 GB) at Q4, all three local tiers recommend `Gemma 4 26B A4B (Reasoning)` at `vram_req=14.87 GB`, headroom 1.13 GB, `fits="yes"` (headroom >= 1.0, line 557) — and the compat chart hover (components/charts/local_compat.py:64-70) prints "VRAM needed: 14.9 GB" immediately above "Context: 256k tokens". Nothing in the Run Local caption (app.py:~690, "see which models fit — with estimated inference speed") discloses the assumption.
user_impact: A user with a 16 GB card follows the recommendation, pulls the 26B model, and OOMs the moment they set a context above roughly 4-8k — the tool promised 256k. On a 24 GB card the tool says Qwen3-32B-class models fit with 4.6 GB to spare when full-context KV alone is 34 GB. This is the single most damaging number on the Run Local tab because it is the one the user acts on before downloading tens of GB.
suggested_fix: Add a `context_tokens` (or fraction-of-max) parameter to `calc_vram_gb` and `get_local_df`, compute KV bytes from per-model `n_layers`/`n_kv_heads`/`head_dim` (add these to the catalog and scraper) plus a KV-quant setting, and fold it into `headroom`. Short of the full model, at minimum surface the assumed context in the chart subtitle and hover ("fits at Nk context") instead of showing the model's max context next to a context-free VRAM figure.
verify_reasoning: Tried to refute by looking for a context term anywhere downstream. `inspect.signature(calc_vram_gb)` is `(params_b: float, quant: str)` and `inspect.signature(get_local_df)` is `(quant, vram_gb, bandwidth_gbps, hw_type, tags)` — no context parameter in either. `'context_k' in inspect.getsource(get_local_df)` is False. Proved independence empirically: for one model at each of the 14 distinct context_k values in the live catalog (8k .. 10000k), `vram_req_gb` equals `params_b * 0.5 * 1.18` to the cent every time — e.g. context_k=10000, params 109.0, vram 64.31 == 64.31. Reproduced the exact UI case: GPU_BY_NAME['NVIDIA RTX 5080'] = 16 GB / 960 GB/s, and all three local tiers return Gemma 4 26B A4B (Reasoning), vram_req_gb 14.87, fits 'yes', context_k 256. Confirmed the hover really juxtaposes them — components/charts/local_compat.py hovertemplate emits 'VRAM needed: %{customdata[2]:.1f} GB' two lines above 'Context: %{customdata[5]}k tokens'. Also confirmed the misleading comment: data/local_models.py:34-35 labels `_OVERHEAD = 1.18` 'KV-cache + activation overhead multiplier', and the module docstring line 9 states the formula is params×bytes×OVERHEAD. Partial refutation of the evidence: the three architectures cited (Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen3 32B, Llama 3.3 70B) are NOT in the live catalog — they only exist in the dead `_MODELS_RAW` fallback (the CSV cache exists, so `_load_models_raw` never reaches it), and the KV byte figures rest on published architectures I cannot execute against. The arithmetic checks out (32L×8kv×128×2×2B×131072 = 17.18 GB) and the direction of error is unarguable, but the headline percentages are not independently verifiable here. Severity lowered to medium: weights×1.18 is the conventional Ollama-style heuristic and the whole tab is labelled 'estimated'; the real defect is the max-context number displayed next to a context-free VRAM figure.

title: Unchecking every provider silently falls back to all 148 models instead of showing an empty state
evidence:
`select_stack` line 424-426:
```
api_pool = df.copy()
if providers:
    api_pool = api_pool[api_pool["provider"].isin(providers)]
```
`[]` is falsy, so "no providers selected" and "all providers" take the same branch. Both callers deliberately distinguish the two — app.py:1041-1048 and static_api.py:381-388 both do `elif not selected: providers = []` as a separate branch from `elif "__all__" in selected: providers = None`, so `[]` was clearly meant to mean "none".

Executed both for every mode:
  api      providers=[]   -> ['DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (Reasoning, Max Effort)', 'DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (Reasoning, Max Effort)', 'Claude Opus 5 (Adaptive Reasoning, Max Effort)']
  api      providers=None -> identical  (IDENTICAL=True)
  hybrid / hybrid2 / local -> identical in every case.
user_impact: A user unchecks Anthropic, Google and OpenAI to see "what if I use none of the big three". The card silently repopulates with Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 in the Reasoning tier. The filter appears to have simply not worked, and worse, the user cannot tell whether the recommendation respects their constraint — every provider chip is still eligible.

(`_tier_card_html` line 654 already handles the empty frame). Keep `None` as the "all providers" sentinel, which both callers already emit for `__all__`.
verify_reasoning: Tried to refute by checking whether a caller intercepts the empty list before it reaches select_stack. It does not — app.py:1043-1049 and static_api.py:379-388 both compute `elif not selected: providers = []` as an explicit branch distinct from `providers = None`, then pass it straight through to build_stack_cards/select_stack. Executed both sentinels for all four modes with the real df (148 rows) and a real local_df: api -> ['DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (Reasoning, Max Effort)', same, 'Claude Opus 5 (Adaptive Reasoning, Max Effort)'] for BOTH [] and None (IDENTICAL True); hybrid, hybrid2 and local likewise IDENTICAL True. The cause is exactly components/stack_recommender.py:425 `if providers:` treating [] as falsy. Verified reachable in both renderings: Dash dcc.Checklist yields [] when all boxes are unchecked, and docs/app.js:596 `Array.from(querySelectorAll('input[name="recommend-providers"]:checked')).map(...)` yields [] identically. Severity lowered to medium: the fallback returns real, correctly-computed recommendations rather than garbage, and some UIs legitimately treat 'none checked' as 'all' — but both callers' code proves [] was meant to mean 'none', so it is a genuine silent failure.

title: Local "Balanced" tier's VRAM-efficiency term is un-normalized and an order of magnitude too small, so Balanced degenerates into "max quality" — identical to Reasoning on 66% of GPU presets
evidence:
`_pick_local_tier`, balanced branch (lines 162-170):
```
runnable["_score"] = ((runnable["quality"] / q_max) * 0.70 +
                      (1 / runnable["vram_req_gb"].replace(0, nan).fillna(99)) * 0.30)
```
The quality term is min-max normalized to [0, 0.70]; the VRAM term is a raw reciprocal in GB, never normalized. Measured the two terms on an RTX 4090 (24 GB, Q4) over the 44 runnable models with quality >= 12:
  q_term range 0.226 .. 0.700   (spread 0.474)
  v_term range 0.0141 .. 0.109  (spread 0.095)
The VRAM term can never overcome even a small quality gap, so the argmax is almost always the argmax of quality — which is exactly the Reasoning tier's sort key (line 172, `sort_values("quality")`).

Swept all 137 GPU presets in `GPUS` at Q4:
  Balanced top pick == Reasoning top pick on 90/137 = 66% of presets
  all three tiers identical on 27/137 = 20%
Swept all six quant levels on a single RTX 4090: Balanced == Reasoning at FP16, Q8, Q5, Q4, Q3 and Q2 — 6/6.
user_impact: On an RTX 4090 the user sees "Balanced — Daily driver" and "Reasoning — Orchestrator" both recommending Qwen3.6 27B (Reasoning), with the Reasoning card advising "Slowest and most expensive — reserve for the top-level orchestrator only" about the model it just told them to use as their daily driver. Two of the three tiers carry no information, and the VRAM-efficiency trade-off the tier claims to make ("quality/VRAM efficiency", module docstring line 11) never actually happens.
suggested_fix: Normalize the VRAM term the same way the quality term is normalized, e.g. `(vram_min / vram_req)` or `1 - (vram_req - vram_min)/(vram_max - vram_min)`, so both live in [0,1] before weighting. Additionally exclude the Reasoning tier's pick from the Balanced candidate pool (or vice versa) so the three tiers are guaranteed distinct when three distinct runnable models exist.
verify_reasoning: Tried to refute by testing whether the un-normalized reciprocal term ever changes the argmax. It sometimes does (47/137 presets differ), but the headline numbers reproduce exactly. Swept all 137 GPUS at Q4 calling `_pick_local_tier` directly: balanced pick == reasoning pick on 90/137 (65.7%), all three tiers identical on 27/137 (19.7%). Swept all six QUANT_LEVELS on GPU_BY_NAME['NVIDIA RTX 4090'] (24 GB, 1008 GB/s): balanced == reasoning at FP16, Q8, Q5, Q4, Q3, Q2 — 6/6. Measured the two terms on that preset's runnable pool: q_term 0.2262..0.7000 (spread 0.4738), v_term 0.0141..0.1091 (spread 0.0950) — matching the finder's figures to four decimals, so the VRAM term's whole dynamic range is ~1/5 of the quality term's. (One inaccuracy: the finder says 44 runnable models with quality>=12; I measure 22. The term ranges are identical so the pool must be the same — the 44 looks like a miscount, and it is not load-bearing.) Verified the default preset is affected, not just the 4090: RTX 5090 (32 GB, the value= default at app.py:701/714) also gives Balanced == Reasoning == Qwen3.6 27B (Reasoning). Severity lowered to medium: no wrong number is displayed and the picks are valid models — the defect is that two of three tiers carry no information plus contradictory advice text.

title: Multi-GPU option multiplies effective memory bandwidth by 1 + 0.85·(n-1), predicting 6.95× single-stream tokens/sec on 8 GPUs
evidence:
`eff_bw = bandwidth_gbps * (1 + (gpu_count - 1) * 0.85) if gpu_count > 1 else bandwidth_gbps` — duplicated verbatim at app.py:1059 (Agent Stack), app.py:1218 (Run Local), static_api.py:316 and static_api.py:403 (the two static-site mirrors). The GPUs dropdown offers ×1/×2/×4/×8 (app.py:714-717, 417-420; docs/index.html:152-155, 252-255).

Executed for Llama-70B-Q4 on RTX 4090 (1008 GB/s):
  ×1 -> eff_bw 1008 GB/s -> 13.4 tok/s
  ×2 -> eff_bw 1865 GB/s -> 24.8 tok/s  (×1.85)
  ×4 -> eff_bw 3578 GB/s -> 47.7 tok/s  (×3.55)
  ×8 -> eff_bw 7006 GB/s -> 93.3 tok/s  (×6.95)

The VRAM side of the same code path (app.py:1055 `vram_gb = vram_per_gpu * num_gpus`) correctly models a *layer-split* deployment — which is what Ollama/llama.cpp do by default. Under layer split the GPUs execute sequentially per token, so single-stream decode throughput is ~unchanged by adding cards (aggregate bandwidth is not usable by one token). Even tensor-parallel serving (vLLM) is sublinear and collapse-limited by the per-token all-reduce, nowhere near 6.95× on 8 consumer cards over PCIe. So the two halves of the same calculation assume mutually incompatible parallelism strategies.
user_impact: A user sizing a local rig sets GPUs=×4 and is told a 70B model will run at 48 tok/s instead of 13 — a purchasing decision on the order of several thousand dollars made against a number that is ~3.5× optimistic for the standard llama.cpp/Ollama setup. Because the identical expression is copy-pasted into four places, fixing one leaves the other three wrong.
suggested_fix: Keep `vram_gb = vram_per_gpu * num_gpus` (correct for layer split) but leave `eff_bw` at the single-card bandwidth, and label the GPUs control as "pools VRAM; does not increase single-stream speed". If tensor parallelism is meant to be modelled, make it an explicit toggle with a realistic curve (~1.6× at 2, ~2.4× at 4) and hoist the expression into one shared helper in data/local_models.py so app.py and static_api.py cannot drift.
verify_reasoning: Tried to refute by checking whether the ×N control is wired to anything real or whether a comment discloses the assumption. `grep -rn '0.85' app.py static_api.py docs/app.js docs/pyworker.js` returns exactly four hits — app.py:1059, app.py:1218, static_api.py:316, static_api.py:403 — all the same bare expression, no comment or caveat anywhere. The ×1/×2/×4/×8 options are confirmed in all four places: app.py:417-419, app.py:713-715, docs/index.html:150-155, docs/index.html:252-257. Executed the real code path for a 70B Q4 model on GPU_BY_NAME['NVIDIA RTX 4090'] (1008 GB/s): ×1 eff_bw 1008 -> 13.4 tok/s; ×2 1865 -> 24.8 (1.85×); ×4 3578 -> 47.7 (3.55×); ×8 7006 -> 93.3 (6.95×) — reproduces the finder's numbers exactly. The internal contradiction is provable from the code alone without appealing to any benchmark: the same three lines (app.py:1055 `vram_gb = vram_per_gpu * num_gpus` and app.py:1059 eff_bw) pool VRAM as if layer-split while summing bandwidth as if tensor-parallel — mutually exclusive deployments. The '~unchanged single-stream throughput under layer split' claim itself is an external modelling assertion I could not execute. Severity lowered to medium: ×1 is the default so the wrong numbers require the user to change a non-default control, and the whole tab is labelled 'estimated inference speed' — but the error reaches 6.95× and is copy-pasted into four files.

title: MoE tokens/sec is computed from active params only, overshooting real llama.cpp throughput by 74-150% and driving the local "Fast" pick
evidence:
`calc_speed_tps` line 498-502: `active_gb = active_b * QUANT_BYTES[quant] * _OVERHEAD; return (bandwidth_gbps / active_gb) * eff`. For MoE rows `active_b` is the routed-expert count only; the always-resident attention, shared-expert, embedding and router weights read on every token are not included, and expert gather is not contiguous.

Formula output on an RTX 4090 (24 GB, 1008 GB/s, Q4) vs published llama.cpp single-stream figures:
  Llama 3.1 8B (dense)          predicted 117.0 tok/s   real ~120-140   -10.0%   ok
  Mistral 7B v0.3 (dense)       predicted 129.8 tok/s   real ~140-160   -13.5%   ok
  Gemma 2 27B (dense)           predicted  34.5 tok/s   real ~38-42     -13.6%   ok
  Qwen 2.5 32B (dense)          predicted  28.6 tok/s   real ~35-40     -23.6%   marginal
  gpt-oss-20b (3.6B active)     predicted 261.0 tok/s   real ~120-180   +74.0%   FAIL
  Qwen3 30B-A3B (3B active)     predicted 313.2 tok/s   real ~100-150  +150.6%   FAIL

The dense predictions are inside the ~20% band; only MoE breaks it. The consequence inside the recommender is concrete: `_pick_local_tier` fast (lines 151-161) weights `speed_tps` at 0.50, and the tool asserts `Qwen3.6 35B A3B (Reasoning)` runs at 313 tok/s vs the dense `Qwen3.6 27B (Reasoning)` at 33.8 tok/s on the same card — a 9.3× gap derived purely from 36B/3B. That number alone makes the A3B model the Fast local pick on every NVIDIA preset I swept.
user_impact: A user picks the MoE model for their Fast tier expecting 313 tok/s and gets roughly a third of that, making the local Fast tier slower than the cloud tier it was supposed to replace. The Run Local compat chart annotates the same inflated figure next to every MoE bar.
suggested_fix: Use an effective read size that includes the non-expert weights, e.g. `read_b = active_b + shared_b` where `shared_b` is scraped or approximated (a common fit is `active_b + 0.15 * params_b` for large-expert-count MoEs), and/or apply a separate lower `eff` for `moe == True` rows calibrated against llama.cpp MoE benchmarks.
verify_reasoning: The code fact is confirmed and I partially REFUTED the evidence. Confirmed: `calc_speed_tps` (data/local_models.py:488-502) computes `active_gb = active_b * QUANT_BYTES[quant] * _OVERHEAD` — active params only, no shared/attention/embedding term. On the 4090 preset at Q4 the live catalog yields gpt-oss-20b 261.0 tok/s (21B total / 3.6B active) and Qwen3.6 35B A3B (Reasoning) 313.2 vs dense Qwen3.6 27B (Reasoning) 33.8 — a 9.3× gap, reproducing the finder's numbers exactly. But the calibration table is built on models that are NOT in the live catalog: I searched the CSV-backed `get_local_df()` for 'Llama 3.1 8B', 'Mistral 7B', 'Gemma 2 27B', 'Qwen 2.5 32B' and 'Qwen3 30B-A3B' — zero matches; all five exist only in `_MODELS_RAW`, the 87-row fallback that `_load_models_raw` never reaches because data/raw/aa_local_models.csv exists. So the '-10.0% / -13.5% / +74.0% / +150.6%' comparison was computed against dead code, and the 'real ~120-140 tok/s' side is external data I cannot execute. I also refuted the sweep claim outright: the A3B model is the Fast local pick on 26 of 48 NVIDIA presets, not 'every NVIDIA preset' — Qwen3.5 4B (Reasoning) wins 14 and Gemma 4 26B A4B (Reasoning) wins 8. The direction of the error is unarguable (active-only read size is a strict underestimate of bytes touched per token) but the magnitude is unverified here.

title: Tier selection can return the identical model for all three tiers with no disclosure, leaving the static advice text self-contradictory
evidence:
`select_stack` (lines 430-465) picks each tier independently from overlapping pools with no cross-tier de-duplication, and `_tier_card_html`/`_tier_card` always print the fixed `_TIER_ADVICE` strings (lines 67-83) regardless of what was picked.
